News.title: Police appeal to find missing teen girl last seen five days ago in Gloucester
News.content:
Police appeal to find missing teen girl last seen five days ago in Gloucester

Leinah, 17, was last seen at around 7.30am on Tuesday with cops exhausting several lines of enquiry before now turning to the public for help finding her

View 2 Images Seventeen-year-old Leinah has been missing for five days (Image: Gloucestershire Police)

People are being asked to dial 999 if they see a teen girl who has been missing for five days.

‌



17-year-old Leinah went missing from Gloucester on Tuesday 21 July, police have said.

‌



She was last seen at around 7.30am and left an address in the Hempstead area on foot shortly afterwards before vanishing with concerns growing for her welfare.

‌



Gloucestershire Police said it has already completed a number of enquiries in the search for the missing teen before now asking for the public's help.

Today the force has appealed for information and released two images citing concerns for Leinah.

‌



View 2 Images She was last seen wearing blue jeans, a black hoodie, white trainers and carrying a small, cream handbag (Image: Gloucestershire Police)

She is described as being around 5ft 2ins tall, of a slim build and with long brown hair which she may be wearing in a ponytail or claw clip.

She was last seen wearing blue jeans, a black hoodie, white trainers and carrying a small, cream handbag.

Article continues below

Anyone who has seen Leinah or knows of her whereabouts is being asked to contact police on 101 quoting reference 53260062654.

Alternatively, if you u can see her at the time of calling, Gloucestershire Police have said to dial 999 instead and ask for police.

News.title: Andy Burnham to meet Volodymyr Zelensky as Ukraine President becomes first world leader to visit PM in UK
News.content:
Andy Burnham to meet Volodymyr Zelensky as Ukraine President becomes first world leader to visit PM in UK

Volodymyr Zelensky and Andy Burnham are going to meet on a British naval base on Monday - as Britain shares vital know-how on how to make state-of-the-art Stone Cloak jammers to prevent Russia tracking drones

View 3 Images Volodymyr Zelensky will become the first world leader to meet Andy Burnham in the UK (Image: PA)

Volodymyr Zelensky will become the first world leader to meet Andy Burnham, as the two hold a crunch meeting in the UK on Monday.

‌



The Ukrainian President is expected to join the Prime Minister at a British naval base, where the PM will share vital know-how to help produce state-of-the-art electronic jammers to block Russian defence systems. This will allow Ukraine to mass produce devices, known as Stone Cloak, to prevent its drones being tracked and targeted.

‌



Mr Burnham described the technology as "the best of homegrown British innovation". He said: "Britain stands with Ukraine, shoulder to shoulder, and our support remains unwavering. Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve, and we will not back down until we achieve long-lasting and just peace for Ukraine.

‌



"Stone Cloak is the best of homegrown British innovation and proven on the frontline, and it will be vital to protecting our security in both our countries."

View 3 Images Andy Burnham said the UK's support for Ukraine remains steadfast (Image: GETTY)

No10 said the UK is sharing the intellectual property for Stone Cloak, which will be built into the next generation of UK deep-strike capabilities. The British military will use the jammers to enhance Project Brakestop - the UK's new low-cost cruise missile. Thousands of the tablet-sized devices have already been gifted to Ukraine to help with drone operations.

‌



No10 said the move knocks Russia a step back in Putin's illegal invasion on Ukraine. During Mr Zelensky's visit, he and Mr Burnham will meet more than 200 Ukrainian military personnel and sailors who have been training in the UK for the past three weeks.

The UK has previously pledged £3billion a year to Ukraine to help fight Russia for as long as it takes - providing a total of £25bn in support since 2022.

It comes as Mr Burnham revealed he was prepared to stand up to Donald Trump, if it were in Britain's national interest. In an interview with the BBC, to be screened in full on Monday, he said: "Well, I've had one phone call. I always treat people as I find them, and it was a good exchange. It was, as I said before, a warm exchange.

‌



View 3 Images Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said he has held talks with his US counterpart (Image: Yui Mok/PA Wire)

"So I am that kind of politician, I always judge people as I find them. I've lived my whole life by that. And I found him to be really warm on Monday. But obviously we will continue to build the relationship as we go forward."

Pressed by journalist Laura Kuenssberg on whether he would be prepared to call out the President if needed, Mr Burnham said: "Of course... all leaders have to do that. You have to defend your own national interest before anything else.

‌



"That's what you're required to do if you're to do this job properly. I will always put Britain's interests first." His predecessor, Keir Starmer, had a difficult relationship with the US President after he refused to allow US forces to use British bases to launch aggressive strikes on Iran.

On Sunday new Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said he had spoken to US counterpart Pete Hegseth, and made clear that position would continue. But he stated the two nations were working together on reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

The vital shipping route, which transports 20% of the world's natural gas and oil supplies, has been effectively shut by Iran after the US and Israel launched attacks on February 28.

‌



Mr Streeting told Sky News: "I was clear that we've not supported offensive action in Iran and we won't support offensive action in Iran, but there are plenty of things that we can and should do together when it comes to securing the Strait of Hormuz, in making sure that Iran doesn't develop nuclear weapons, in terms of investing in our capability and Nato's capability."

He said the closure is having a big economic impact and admitted: "But it's hard to undertake that work, of clearing the strait and securing commercial shipping while hostilities continue. And that's why every effort is being made, particularly by allies in the region, to try and bring about the conditions where we can achieve that."

Describing relations with the Trump administration he said: "The first thing you do is you don't suck up. And I don't think, my impression is, President Trump, his administration, that's not what they're looking for, actually. He's a straight talker."

Article continues below

Asked if he trusts the US President, the Defence Secretary said: "Well, I don't know him, but I do trust the United States." He said the relationship between the two nations is unlike any in the world.

At the weekend John Healey, the new Chancellor, promised a "buy British" blitz within the UK government. He told The Sun: "You will see this as a determined drive that you have not seen before from a British government. Buying British not 'if possible', but by design. So every procurement pound supports British jobs, British apprenticeships and British skills."

He pointed out that when he was Defence Secretary, over 86% of the 1,200 major defence contracts handed out went to British firms. The government is yet to set a timetable for reaching 3% of the UK's gross domestic product (GDP) on defending the nation. Mr Healey told the Sun this was "not a matter for this first week".

News.title: Cruel owner made three dogs live in house of horror in smashed glass and broken furniture
News.content:
Cruel owner made three dogs live in house of horror in smashed glass and broken furniture

Connor Stewart pleaded guilty to breaching animal welfare legislation after his three dogs were found living in "appalling" conditions and were underweight with visible ribs showing

View 3 Images The three dogs were found underweight and living in horrific conditions (Image: SSPCA)

A cruel pet owner made his three dogs live among smashed glass and broken furniture until they were rescued.

‌



The poor pups had no access to food and water, and their living conditions were described as "appalling" by animal welfare groups. Their owner, Connor Stewart, pleaded guilty to breaching animal welfare legislation.

‌



It was clear the dogs' living conditions were horrendous, even when Scottish SPCA inspectors looked through the letterbox of the Livingstone home. Stewart was told to return to the flat and give them access and, after arriving, brought Dobermans Ammo and Karma and Staffordshire Bull Terrier Kya out onto the landing area.

‌



View 3 Images The dogs lived in filthy conditions (Image: Scottish SPCA/PA Wire)

Anyone who spots stray cats on holiday urged to do one thing READ MORE :

Ammo was underweight, with his ribs and hips obviously visible and his nails overgrown. An inspector said: "The flat was completely squalid. The floors were soaked in urine and covered in thick layers of faeces throughout the property, some of which was beginning to turn mouldy. There was broken furniture throughout, smashed glass on the floors and electric shock collars charging in the kitchen area of the flat.

‌



"All the food and water bowls were empty and bone dry." These conditions were some of the worst the inspector had found animals living in and the decision was made to remove all dogs from the property and take them into the care of the Scottish SPCA.

View 3 Images The floors were soaked in urine and covered in layers of faeces (Image: Scottish SPCA/PA Wire)

Police Scotland were called to support removal of the animals, but Stewart fled with his two Dobermans. His remaining Staffordshire Bull Terrier, Kya was taken to a local veterinary practice for further care.

Article continues below

The poor pooch smelled strongly of urine and faeces and drank voraciously having had no water. After pleading guilty, Stewart was sentenced last week and has been banned from owning, keeping or caring for animals for five years. He was also fined £200.

The inspector added: "We are pleased with the Sheriff's decision. Stewart's behaviour was unacceptable, and he showed complete disregard for his dogs' wellbeing.

"No animal should be kept in such conditions, and we hope this sentencing sends a clear message that animal neglect will not be tolerated in Scotland."

News.title: 'Future of Andy Burnham's mission to transform Britain rests on dodging Starmer's destructive defence targets'
News.content:
Ruinous rises for a spendthrift Ministry of Defence are a bullet Andy Burnham and John Healey either dodge or Labour’s fresh commanders will shoot a revitalised UK government in the foot.

Because the blunt choice is between prioritising higher living standards, social care and council houses or throwing away good money after bad without any proof Britain would be better protected militarily. The new Prime Minister signalled he’s spotted the trap in refusing to commit to predecessor Keir Starmer’s £80billion annual target of 3% GDP by 2030, up £10bn a year, in his BBC interview.

For Healey, now charged with finding money after quitting as Starmer’s Defence Secretary with an incendiary claim the country wasn’t safe, the dilemma is deeply personal as well as highly political. Stick to Starmer’s destructive Nato 3.5% guns and that would soar to £140bn by 2035, requiring a £40bn increase in today’s prices. The respected Institute for Government think-tank warned that is the equivalent to two-thirds of the schools budget or the combined budgets of the Home Office and Ministry of Justice.

View 4 Images Andy Burnham (Image: Paul Marriott/Shutterstock)

‌



Streeting says he wouldn't have accepted Defence Secretary job without Burnham spending promise READ MORE :

Welfare vs warfare may over-simplify options but unless the PM and Chancellor find a giant pot of gold there would be trade-offs. And unless a political-industrial-military consensus (all major national parties save the Greens are locked in a ludicrous game of Play Your Cards Right shouting “higher”) is challenged an MoD damned for “unbelievable” waste by decorated Colonel Al Carns who resigned alongside Healey will be a disastrous drain.

We need Burnham to state Britain is already the world’s sixth biggest defence spender and towards the head of the Nato pack in share of national wealth. The basic idea of Nato is Britain never stands alone which is a double relief given the MoD’s record of paying more for late and worse armoured vehicles and warships.

My hunch is the PM will duck and dive rather than disown Starmer’s legacy of unrealistic, unnecessary international targets as he tries to fill a £5bn black hole. For Healey, it’s much tricker, though he could drop into conversations the 500,000 men GCHQ spy centre’s chiefs believes Russia has lost in Ukraine means Putin’s bled his country dry.

One of Burnham’s new ministers told me the percentage targets were madness. The PM might agree.

‌



The future of his mission to transform Britain for everybody rests on missing them.

Farage's pop-up prison hypocrisy

Had to laugh when flailing Farage proposed pop-up “Nightingale” prisons on MoD land to ease overcrowding when kneejerk Nigel and Reform routinely back locals campaigning against holding asylum seekers in redundant army camps.

I don’t imagine villagers and townies would welcome thousands of criminals plopped on their doorsteps in makeshift, insecure huts and I bet hypocritical Farage would join the outrage.

View 4 Images Farage's 'Nightingale' hypocrisy (Image: James Veysey/Shutterstock)

‌



Burnham, who is reviewing who might be let out early to free cells for fresh convicts, inherited a poisonous Sophie’s Choice from the Con-servatives which bedevilled Starmer but this is an issue exposing Reform’s vacuous gimmickry.

Running away from debating a bin in his Clacton farce, Farage wants to talk about everything except his £5million secret bung, aristo “Posh George” Cottrell paying his bills and now London private bank Arbuthnot Latham freezing Reform’s account for two weeks during the general election over potentially illegal donations.

Fleet is the real deal

Burnham enjoyed a sure-footed first week but one misstep was not finding a new job for Natalie Fleet, the Bolsover MP whose own rape traumas prevented her from continuing as Safeguarding Minister.

Groomed, raped and made pregnant aged 15 by an older man and revealing she was raped in her sleep by another, the strength she finds to speak publicly is heroic.

‌



View 4 Images Natalie Fleet is the real deal

That Fleet doesn’t consider herself brave or courageous is another reason this working class marvel who speaks for and inspires millions of other women feeling ignored should’ve been shuffled into another post. Be it making welfare work, sorting social care or building houses, the point is we need people not robots in power – and fighter Fleet is the real deal.

Inciting the dross

No great surprise most thugs arrested during last month’s mindless violence after the jailing of student Henry Nowak’s cynical murderer had previously been reported to police for domestic abuse.

I say no great surprise because two in five arrested after summer 2024 disturbances in parts of the country following the Southport murders had similarly been reported for domestic abuse.

‌



Hard Right and Far Right politicians incite the dross to riot. Entirely separately, have you heard their deafening silence since the arrest of influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate on 59 charges of rape, violent assault, trafficking girls and the indecent images of a child? Bet it would be a different story if they were Muslims.

Going Up

Brickie turned Liverpool City Region Mayor Steve Rotheram is the most important building block in Andy Burnham’s team.

As long as these Scousers stay friends the new PM’s feet are on the ground. Fall out and it’ll be like the ravens leaving the Tower of London.

Going Down

Blocked standing again for the Cons by Kemi Badenoch because she doesn’t think him extreme enough, ex-party chair Grant Shapps should reapply under his get-rich-quick pseudonym Michael Green. The Tories always love a scammer.

News.title: Berlin Pride crash updates: Suspect shot dead by police after terror attack
News.content:
Berlin attack shows why Pride is still necessary, Streeting says

Wes Streeting says last night's attack shows why Pride marches are necessary.

The defence secretary said incidents like yesterday's are "becoming far too common on our television screens".

"I would say to people, especially at a time when Pride marches have come in for some challenge: why do we have Pride marches? Why are they necessary in this country? Hasn't this all changed?," Streeting told Sky News.

"In many respects, things are different and better now than they've ever been [...] But hate crimes are also on the rise. There are lots of people who don't accept diversity and difference in our society.

Wes Streeting (file image) (Image: SKY NEWS)

"And that's why pride is a celebration. But it's also a protest against those who do not accept life in the 21st century, do not accept people loving each other in same-sex relationships and in the very worst cases would seek to do us harm."

Asked about possible threats to the upcoming Brighton Pride parade, he added that the event would be "well policed" and "get the balance right in terms of policing".

"The home secretary will [...] make the right determinations around what kind of policing presence we need," he said.

News.title: Berlin Pride suspect shot dead by police after man 'rams van into crowd with 1 killed and 16 injured'
News.content:
Berlin Pride suspect shot dead by police after man 'rams van into crowd with 1 killed and 16 injured'

The attack occurred at round 10pm on Saturday a few hundred yards from a party near the Brandenburg Gate that was supposed to close out the city’s Pride festival, as a white van drove into the Tiergarten Park and hit several people in a crowd

View 6 Images 21-year old suspect identified by police as Abdul Ballout (Image: POLIZEI BERLIN/AFP via Getty Images)

German police have shot dead the man suspected of driving a van into a crowd near Berlin’s Pride festival, killing a woman and injuring at least 29 people.

‌



Alleged terrorist Abdul Ballout, 21, rushed at police with a weapon before being shot by cops, officials said. The suspect was tracked down to an allotment garden in Spandau, West Berlin.

‌



Authorities had previously issued a wanted notice and warned people against approaching Ballout, a German citizen with Lebanese roots, saying he may be armed and dangerous.

‌



View 6 Images Heavily-armed police stand in a garden where they reportedly confronted and shot dead Abdul Ballout (Image: Getty Images)

Berlin Pride attack: All we know as manhunt for suspect Abdul Ballout continues READ MORE :

Four men killed in Merseyside crash named as heartbroken families pay tribute READ MORE :

Polizei Berlin said last night: “At around 6pm, the suspect in yesterday’s attack in the Grosser Tiergarten was located in an allotment garden in Spandau.

“He is said to have rushed toward our emergency forces with a stabbing weapon, after which police firearms were used.

‌



View 6 Images The van that allegedly was driven into people killing one person and injuring 16 before crashing on a tree (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

“Despite immediate resuscitation measures, he died at the scene.” Witnesses reported hearing two volleys of gunfire a few minutes apart during the raid on the garden shed. Berlin’s ­interior senator Iris Spranger thanked the police, saying: “I am grateful to the security authorities for finding the attacker so quickly.”

View 6 Images Emergency personnel and police work near the scene last night (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Earlier, interior minister Alexander Dobrindt said the suspect had come to the authorities’ attention in the past because of numerous crimes and “radicalisation and belonging to the Islamist scene” in the German capital. He added: “Everything we see here points to us dealing with an Islamic terror attack.”

View 6 Images Mourners in front of the Brandenburg Gate near the scene (Image: CLEMENS BILAN/EPA/Shutterstock)

The attack occurred at round 10pm on Saturday a few hundred yards from a party near the Brandenburg Gate that was supposed to close out the city’s Pride festival.

Article continues below

According to police, a white van drove into the Tiergarten Park and hit several people in a crowd that was likely to be a mix of festival goers and other visitors before colliding with a tree.

View 6 Images People wrapped in security blankets hug near the scene (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Briton Ashley Jump, 26, attended Saturday’s parade but left before the attack. They returned yesterday to leave flowers at a memorial. Ashley said: “They’ll never erase us, we’ll never be gone. As long as humanity has existed, we’ve existed. We will not be removed.”

News.title: British expat's France home 'smells like really strong burning' as entire city has smokey stench
News.content:
British expat's France home 'smells like really strong burning' as entire city has smokey stench

EXCLUSIVE: Holidaymakers have been urged to avoid visiting Bordeaux and the surrounding area, after thousands of people were evacuated away from a massive and "unpredictable" wildfire near the iconic French city

View 5 Images Firefighters continue to battle the blaze that is advancing toward Bordeaux (Image: SDIS33 - Caporal-chef Damien Rembert/AFP via Getty Images)

A British expat has revealed her Bordeaux flat smells "like really strong burning" as the wildfire advances to within nine miles of the French city.

‌



Karen Kissane, 51, from Newcastle, was on holiday in Barcelona when the terrifying news about firefighters struggling to contain a wildfire near her home of the past six years. After returning to Bordeaux from holiday, Karen described the city as feeling "eerie" and filled with the pungent smell of smoke.

‌



She told the Mirror: "We will be getting out just to get some fresh air, because, of course, the fires are a worry, but the air quality and the breathing it in is not pleasant as well. I mean, in my apartment right now it smells of burning inside .

‌



View 5 Images Karen said she was prepared to leave Bordeaux at short notice (Image: Karen Kissane)

Georgia Toffolo emotional as she reveals she fled Cap Ferret by boat to escape wildfires READ MORE :

First victim of Spanish wildfires found as 270k people flee their homes READ MORE :

"The windows are closed, the doors are closed, and it smells like really strong burning inside my apartment, which we all have to sleep with. When I opened the front door, there was ash in the doorway. So, there's obviously ash particles in the air as well."

Karen had been unsure about whether to return home after she filtered through contradictory information online and made the decision earlier to catch the flight back to Bordeaux.

‌



" When I got off the plane and walked down the steps, the smell of burning in the air really hit me, um, and it just felt really hot and humid, and there was wind in the air that was blowing the burning smell around," business strategist Karen added.

"I could really sense that the fires could spread quickly because of the breeze. I have an apartment in the centre of Bordeaux, and I'm looking out the window now, and it's all white outside." Karen described the felling in Bordeaux as "strange" with quiet streets during peak tourist season in the picturesque French city.

View 5 Images Smoke from the wildfire had turned the sky a shade of white (Image: Karen Kissane)

‌



While the horror scenes she had seen on TV were not a reflection of the situation in the heart of the city, an unease continued to hang in the air. "I was driving back to my apartment, which is in the centre of Bordeaux, just on the river, and it just felt strange. It felt like there was something not right."

French firefighters are struggling to contain massive blazes following a streak of three heatwaves in the country already this summer with another predicted for next week. A total of 65,000 to 70,000 British citizens live across the southern regions of France, making up roughly 43 per cent of the country's total British population

Holidaymakers have been urged to stay away from Bordeaux amid ongoing evacuations in nearby areas. Sadly, it is a similar story across much of southern Europe, with fires blazing across parts of Spain, Italy as well as England and Scotland.

‌



Sophie Brocas, the prefect for Nouvelle-Aquitaine, said: "We urge tourists not to come to this region, at least until the situation is under control. I encourage tourists who are already here to consider another destination."

View 5 Images Many people were forced to flee their homes (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Karen said she will be constantly monitoring the situation around Bordeaux and will take her two children, aged 14 and 16, to a holiday property about an hour and a half north of the city should the situation suddenly change. The mum said she "wouldn't hesitate" to make a fast decision.

‌



"My priority is the safety of my kids and, at this moment in time, no one really knows what can happen over the coming days, and that's part of the problem," she said. "The unpredictability is very difficult to plan for."

"It could get better, or it could get a whole lot worse, and I don't like that feeling of not knowing. With the breeze I mentioned, you can see how suddenly it can take hold, and head in a different direction or get worse."

View 5 Images Fires continued to rage around Bordeaux (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Article continues below

Karen revealed some of her friends were forced to leave their holiday homes in nearby Cap Ferret as firefighters battled to contain the fire. She added: "I do have some friends who have holiday properties in Cap Ferret and the areas that are worst hit, and they've been evacuated. I know of people who were evacuated at 3am, and they literally had to pick everything up and leave. For anyone who's holidaying in that area, it's an, it's an absolute no-go."

The Foreign Office said in new travel advice issued on Sunday: "French authorities have evacuated campsites, tourist accommodation and some residential areas. Access to affected areas may be restricted and roads may close at short notice. Further evacuations may take place.

"If you are in an affected area, or planning to travel there: follow instructions and updates from local authorities and emergency services at all times, and call 112 if you need emergency help. Check with your accommodation or travel provider before travelling."

News.title: Man dies after getting into difficulty in sea off West Wittering beach
News.content:
Man dies after getting into difficulty in sea off West Wittering beach

A man has died this afternoon after getting into trouble in the sea at West Wittering beach near Portsmouth - emergency services were called to reports of two adults in difficulty

View Image Rescuers at West Wittering Beach (Image: eddie mitchell)

A man has died after he got into trouble in the sea at a popular beach off the south coast.

‌



Emergency services were called to West Wittering beach with reports of two adults in the water near the Beach Café on Sunday afternoon.

‌



Two men were pulled from the sea with paramedics treating both. But despite the best efforts of medics, one of the men was pronounced dead at the scene.

‌



In a statement, Sussex Police said: "Emergency services were called to the beach near the Beach Café, Pound Road, West Wittering, around 2.30pm on Sunday, 26 July, after two adults got into difficulty in the water.

"Both were pulled from the sea and received treatment from emergency services at the scene. Sadly, one of the men was pronounced dead at the scene. The other man has been taken to hospital as a precaution.

"The men are not believed to be known to each other. Next of kin have been informed and the matter has been passed to the coroner’s officer."

‌



In a post on Facebook, West Wittering Beach administrators said: "We are deeply saddened to confirm that a 55-year-old man has sadly passed away following an incident at West Wittering Beach today.

"Our lifeguards responded immediately and together with the ambulance service, coastguard and other emergency services, provided advanced first aid and CPR.

"Despite their best efforts, he was sadly pronounced deceased. The circumstances surrounding this incident are currently being established, and it would be inappropriate to speculate at this time.

‌



"Our thoughts and sincere condolences are with the man's family, friends and all those affected by this tragic incident. We would like to thank our lifeguards, emergency service colleagues and members of the public who assisted during the response. We respectfully ask that the privacy of the family is respected at this incredibly difficult time."

West Wittering has become a popular haunt for the rich and famous with its selection of beachfront mansions. The beach is so in demand that visitors now have to book online just to secure a parking spot when visiting the iconic spot.

The Mirror has launched the Save Lives For Sam water safety campaign to tackle the UK's growing drowning crisis. Backed by MPs, Olympic champions, national water safety organisations and bereaved families, the campaign is calling for urgent action to make our waters safer.

Article continues below

That includes compulsory water safety lessons in schools, a nationwide public awareness campaign, better lifesaving equipment at high-risk waterways, the introduction of Sam's Law, and a dedicated Minister for Water Safety. Find out more about the campaign and how you can support it here.

News.title: Badenoch says PM must rule out tax rises to fund social care reform
News.content:
Kemi Badenoch has written to the prime minister asking him to "rule out any tax rises or increased borrowing" to fund social care reform.

In a letter to Andy Burnham, the Conservative Party leader said she would be happy to work with him to find a solution, but only if he sticks to her party's "two core principles".

She said any reform must be funded by reducing current spending and not raising taxes, and also be fair to those who have "made provisions and saved up over the course of their lives".

Burnham is expected to make a speech on adult social care this week. A No 10 source said this was part of his plan to "run towards problems that have been neglected".

News.title: Trump paused attacks on Iran to make space for talks, US ambassador says
News.content:
President Donald Trump has paused attacks on Iran for the second night in a row to give diplomacy more time, the US ambassador to the UN said.

Speaking to Fox News on Sunday, ambassador Mike Waltz said the president was "giving talks some space, he's giving it a little bit of room".

An Iranian army spokesperson said on Sunday that Tehran had halted "retaliatory" attacks in the region in response.

The pause follows nearly two weeks of daily US strikes and tit-for-tat attacks, effectively unravelling the ceasefire struck in June.

Asked whether Trump had decided against escalation for now, Waltz told NBC: "I wouldn't go that far at all. The president is keeping all options on the table."

Waltz also rejected reports in the New York Times, external that administration officials had warned expanding hostilities could dangerously drain a diminished stockpile of air defence munitions.

"The US military... has everything that it needs to conduct this campaign as effectively as it needs to be," he said.

As of Sunday evening, Trump had not spoken publicly on the latest developments, but earlier posted computer-generated images on his Truth Social account that depicted US military planes bombing Iranian ships and Kharg island.

Meanwhile, Iran and Oman held several rounds of technical talks in Tehran on Friday and Saturday to discuss management of the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei.

Disputes over control of the strait reignited US-Iran tensions earlier this month and it remains a major block to permanently ending the war.

Iran and the US signed a memorandum of understanding in June to halt military operations and reopen the strait, as well as to reach an agreement to end the war over the following 60 days.

But after Iranian forces attacked tankers in the Strait of Hormuz on 13 July, the US resumed airstrikes on the country and reinstated its naval blockade on Iranian ports.

Iran retaliated with attacks on US military facilities and bases across the Middle East, killing four American soldiers. The US strikes have since killed dozens of people, according to Iran's health ministry.

In the UK, new Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said he would meet his US counterpart Pete Hegseth in the coming week to discuss the strait, which is one of the world's key transport routes for oil, liquid natural gas and other essential commodities.

"When it comes to securing maritime freedom and free commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, that's where we are absolutely aligned," Streeting told the BBC.

Earlier this week, oil prices hit $100 a barrel for the first time since May, as the renewed fighting stoked fears over global energy supplies.

As the war nears its fifth month, it remains largely unpopular in the US, with a new poll from CBS/YouGov suggesting 57% of Americans are frustrated about the conflict and only 19% optimistic.

Thousands of people have been killed across the Middle East since the US-Israeli war with Iran began in February, official figures show, with the vast majority coming from Iran and Lebanon.

President Trump is set to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the White House on Tuesday.

News.title: Pogacar wins fifth Tour as Van der Poel takes stage
News.content:
Slovenian Tadej Pogacar won the Tour de France for a record-equalling fifth time.

The 27-year-old UAE Team Emirates-XRG rider crossed the line on Paris' Champs-Elysees in the peloton, to join Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault and Miguel Indurain as the endurance event's most successful male riders.

All-conquering Pogacar raised the idea that his remarkable reality is proving stranger than fiction, describing it as "something you wouldn't even maybe write in a story book".

The three-week Grand Tour's final stage was won by the Netherlands' Mathieu van der Poel of Alpecin-Premier Tech after a frantic charge to the line on the French capital's famous cobbles in which he pipped team-mate Jasper Philipsen of Belgium by inches.

Pogacar's victory means he is positioned by many as the greatest cyclist of all time, superseding the achievements and status of Belgian legend Merckx.

It also marks Pogacar's third Tour win in succession and includes a record-breaking ascent of the iconic Alpe d'Huez on stage 19, when he sealed another dominant victory.

It was the last of five stage wins in a race in which Pogacar used his explosive launch and unmatchable metronomic pace to see off his rivals, who for some time have had virtually no answer.

Pogacar has won almost every major race in the sport, including the Tour of Flanders, Giro d'Italia, Milan-San Remo, Road World Championships, Giro di Lombardia and Liege-Bastogne-Liege.

Pogacar was booed by some fans during the Tour, as his performances are often so far ahead of any of his peers that some feel frustrated the sport is losing its competitive edge.

He now has 127 wins in an eight-year elite professional career.

"Victory is really special," said Pogacar. "Thank you to all the fans and my team.

"But the biggest thanks goes to all my family who support me all my life. My parents - without them I would not be standing here five times already.

"Seven Tours and seven times on the podium, and five wins, is something you wouldn't even maybe write in a story book, and it's unbelievable for me.

"It's a magnificent podium with some incredible champions to fight with.

"It's a shame Jonas [Vingegaard] crashed out this time and many others. I hope they have a quick recovery and next year we fight again."

News.title: Burnham says he is prepared to call out Trump 'if right for Britain'
News.content:
Burnham said: "My strength is remaining close to people, close to the public, that will not change as prime minister."

Asked if he would call out Trump if it was the right thing, he said, "of course", going on to say: "You have to defend your own national interest before anything else. That's what you're required to do if you're to do this job properly."

Burnham also said he had had "concern" about the president starting the conflict with Iran, and he "wouldn't hold back from saying what I think is right".

Responding to Burnham's comments, Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: "Clearly, the US is a long standing ally. We need to have good relations with them but if they do something we disagree with, we should honestly say so."

The prime minister would not commit to a date when the government would spend 3% of GDP on defence. His Chancellor John Healey resigned from the previous government saying that unless a commitment was made to spend that amount by 2030, the country would not be safe.

But Burnham said: "I appointed my new chancellor very aware of what he had said about the critical importance of defence spending and the position that he had taken about that.

"The first challenge facing us both is to ensure that the defence investment plan is fully funded and that's the thing that's right in front of us and we need to work that through as we go towards the budget later this year."

News.title: Four people including baby die after car crash
News.content:
Four people, including a baby, have died after a car crashed into trees on a busy dual carriageway in Derby.

Emergency services were called after a red Hyundai car left the A38 and crashed into trees - between the A50 Toyota Island and the A516 - at about 23:00 BST on Saturday.

Derbyshire Police said the passengers, two women, 18 and 30, and a man, 36, died at the scene. The baby girl was taken to hospital where she died shortly after.

The force said the driver, a 33-year-old man, was arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving. He was subsequently taken to hospital for serious injuries.

Police said all those involved were from Leeds in West Yorkshire, adding their relatives have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.

"Our thoughts are with them at this most distressing time," a spokesperson said.

The carriageway was closed for several hours while emergency services dealt with the crash, but it has since been reopened.

Anyone who witnessed the crash or has any dashcam footage has been urged to contact police.

News.title: Water returns to Gatwick Airport after major outage
News.content:
Gatwick Airport says its water supply has returned after passengers faced long queues for toilets and closed restaurants and bars after a major supply outage.

Both terminals at the UK's second busiest airport lost running water on Sunday morning after a power failure at a treatment works that serves the area.

People told the BBC of confusion and frustration as all bars and restaurants were shut, some were left with nowhere to sit and waits built up outside toilets.

SES Water, the company that supplies the airport, said earlier the power outage was fixed, with Gatwick reporting on Sunday night that water had returned to "the vast majority of the London Gatwick campus".

The water company, which also supplies parts of Kent, Surrey and south London, said complications caused by a power outage at Bough Beech treatment works meant some customers had experienced low water pressure or a temporary loss of supply.

A spokesperson had earlier confirmed that Gatwick Airport was affected.

On Sunday afternoon, SES Water said its treatment works were back up and running, but later added it would take time for the network to fully return to normal as it had been "a highly unusual and complex issue".

"We want to reiterate that our teams are working as quickly as they possibly can and we are grateful for everyone's patience," the spokesperson added.

Gatwick apologised and said staff had been handing out bottled water.

A spokesperson added: "Our staff are on hand to support passengers and provide assistance where needed, some restaurant partners have opened to provide additional seating."

Gatwick said additional teams had been deployed across both terminals to support passengers.

The airport added there had been no flight cancellations as a result of the supply issues and that it was working closely with SES Water to minimise the impact.

"Our teams are working hard to reopen toilets and other facilities as quickly and safely as possible," a spokesperson said.

News.title: Meghan calls Harry 'a charmer' during MasterChef Australia appearance
News.content:
Early on in the episode, Meghan was asked what her favourite dish is to make at home.

She said it was "a tough one because I have a lot of palettes to appease", with her British-born husband favouring "meat, potatoes and cream sauce" while she preferred grilled fish.

Their two children, Archie and Lilibet, often help with meal preparation and are "great eaters", she said.

"We're really lucky on that front," she added.

She then urged the chefs to cook something they felt connected to. "What's the story behind it?" she asked them.

When Prince Harry dialled in later on during the episode, Meghan told them: "My husband's here," prompting cheers and shocked faces from contestants and spectators.

"I wish you could try these, these dishes are fantastic," she told him, before showing him the food. He signed off by telling her to go and enjoy, adding: "Very sorry to disturb you."

The duchessâs appearance on the latest season of the show was well received by Hello Magazine, external, which shared a video of the episode online and complimented Meghan for the way she interacted with the chefs.

"The Duchess of Sussex gave personal time calls to all the contestants, proving that she's always so effortlessly elegant," it wrote.

Writing in The Sunday Times, external, Charlotte Ivers was less impressed, saying her appearance on the show "told us nothing about what she likes or who even will leave the competition".

Social media users were also split, with one viewer writing that Meghan was "warm, gracious and a delight to watch" while another called Prince Harry's cameo appearance "cringe".

News.title: Evans steps out of shadows into spotlight with Scotland's fourth gold
News.content:
Given Evans qualified fastest - and fastest by a distance - any pre-Games ignorance had already evaporated by the time she strode out into this clammy, claustrophic cauldron of noise on Sunday.

The Cambridge-born athlete could have represented England or Wales through her parents but, after choosing to train at the University of Stirling upon her return from studying in the United States, she opted for Scotland.

And the noise that greeted her before - and carried her through - her race was rich reward for that decision.

As Evans' impressive nails - adorned with Saltires, the T of a well-known lager brand, Nessie, and the words 'Irn Bru' - sliced through the water, the crowd grew louder and louder, culminating in a huge wave of noise when she touched the wall.

Afterwards, she confessed to wondering during the race why she didn't feel more stressed but also thanks the Scottish fans for helping her during the tickly bit.

"It's not the biggest crowd I've competed in front of, but it's the loudest and the most passionate," added Evans, who was sixth in this event at the Paris Olympics. "I felt their energy and love especially in the last five metres when it hurt.

"I had the choice of England, Wales or Scotland but Scotland felt right, it felt like home. They made me the athlete I am today and I dreamed of getting a gold and having the crowd roar and this is that but 100 times bigger."

Alarmingly for her rivals, Evans' main event is still to come. The 200m on Wednesday was considered pre-meet a more likely medal prospect for her.

So could she find herself revelling in the Tollcross atmosphere once more?

"I don't think you can top how that felt tonight but we'll see how it goes," she said.

News.title: Andy Burnham rules out early election in exclusive BBC interview
News.content:
In an exclusive interview with the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg, Andy Burnham explicitly dismissed the idea of an early general election, saying "I'm going to rule it out... I don't think people want it."

Explaining his decision, the new prime minister suggested the majority of the electorate "voted for a manifesto" in the last election, and vowed he would "honour that manifesto" with the support of parliamentary colleagues.

Burnham went on to say, "I just think what I most need to do is get Britain focused on getting the country back where it should be, getting it working."

Andy Burnham: The Laura Kuenssberg Interview will be available across BBC News on Sunday and the interview will be shown in full on Panorama on BBC One on Monday at 20:00 BST.

News.title: Teen charged over record crossing on 'mega dinghy'
News.content:
A teenager charged over a small boat Channel crossing was allegedly piloting a "mega dinghy" carrying a record 165 migrants from France to England, the National Crime Agency has said.

Sudanese national Chan Mathok Atak, 19, is accused of endangering another during a journey by sea to the UK on Thursday and is due to appear at Margate Magistrates' Court on Monday.

The number on the dinghy broke the previous record from July, when 128 crossed the Channel from France on one vessel.

According to Home Office figures, more than 13,000 arrivals have been recorded in 2026, which is 45% lower than this time in 2025 and down 18% on the same period in 2024.

Border Security Command was pictured towing a dinghy - estimated to be about the same size as a standard bus at 13m (42ft) long - when it arrived in Dover in Kent on Thursday afternoon.

Home Office figures showed 366 people arrived after crossing in three boats on Thursday during warm, sunny weather and calm conditions at sea.

On Wednesday, 172 people made the journey in three boats, bringing an end to an 11-day hiatus because of windy conditions in the Channel.

Refugee charity Care4Calais said the crossing route was becoming "more and more dangerous" because of the increasing number of people in each boat.

News.title: It's me, Cathy – thousands pay tribute to Kate Bush classic
News.content:
The sun may be hiding behind grey clouds, but for hundreds of people in flowing red dresses dancing on Yorkshire moorland it'll take more than a threat of rain to dampen their spirits.

This is BrontÃ« country, after all, so it's fitting that it's also perfect BrontÃ« weather.

The group, swaying in unison, have come together to re-create the music video for Kate Bush's 1978 song Wuthering Heights, inspired by Emily BrontÃ«'s novel.

Every year, thousands of people around the world don red robes â and in some cases long black wigs â for The Most Wuthering Heights Day Ever.

Events have previously taken place in places such as Sydney, Copenhagen, Berlin, Folkestone and Preston.

This particular "Mass Wuther" perhaps has an even stronger claim than most â it's held on Penistone Hill, not far from the famous BrontÃ« parsonage in Haworth, in the Pennines.

From the field on a clear day can be seen the ruined farmhouse of Top Withens, believed to be the inspiration for the titular farmhouse of BrontÃ«'s novel.

News.title: Iran's 'sabre-rattling' should not intimidate UK, Wes Streeting says
News.content:
When asked if Iran had the capability to attack the UK, Streeting said: "I think we shouldn't put too much stock in the sabre-rattling of Iran, and we certainly shouldn't be intimidated by what the regime has said this week".

He also repeated the UK's position from the outset of the US war against Iran saying "we have not joined and will not join offensive US military action in Iran.

"That's an area where we have not agreed with the United States, but when it comes to securing maritime freedom and free commercial shipping in the straight Hormuz, that's where we are absolutely aligned".

Streeting said he is to meet with US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth in the coming week after "kicking around" ideas for ways "to bring the countries together" and had been "delighted" to speak to Hegseth by phone already.

He also said that the UK is ready to lead a naval mission to help remove mines from the Strait of Hormuz "when the conditions are right".

Securing safe shipping routes through the area was important because of the impact the crisis is having on energy prices and the cost of living, he added.

Streeting also dismissed a Russian warship's recent live-firing exercise in the English Channel as "performative" but added it was a "reminder of the frankly unsafe and unprofessional way in which they have been conducting themselves".

Branding the Channel incident "irresponsible", Streeting said Russia posed a threat to UK security, adding that the public does not see "the enormous efforts that take place every day to counter Russian aggression".

News.title: Family tributes to four men who died in crash
News.content:
The families of four men who died after a car hit a lamp-post on Merseyside have paid tribute to them.

The black Seat Cupra had been travelling from Liverpool towards Knowsley, before it came off the road and crashed on Liverpool Road, Huyton, just before 02:00 BST on Friday.

Jack Diggle, 23, Benjamin Dooley, 23, Andrew Roberts, 24, and Craig Shackleton-Brady, 26, all died at the scene, Merseyside Police said.

Officers are continuing to appeal for information about what happened.

The families of all four men released their tributes together through police.

Jack Diggle's mum said: "Jack was kind, quiet, thoughtful and loving. He adored his family, and we loved him with all our hearts.

"Jack was blessed with a wonderful group of friends, many of whom had been by his side for most of his life.

"He loved playing football with them and was a proud Everton supporter.

"Jack and I went out for a meal together on Thursday. It was such a lovely time, just mother and son, enjoying each other's company. Little did I know that it would be the last time we would spend together.

"Our Jack, our gentle giant, we love you beyond words and will love you forever. Rest peacefully, son."

News.title: Another UK heatwave looms after cooler end to weekend
News.content:
Sunday will be a cooler day for the whole of the UK as temperatures fall widely by a couple of degrees.

A few locations will finally mark the end to their third heatwave of the year, including Usk in Monmouthshire and Exeter in Devon.

Both places are forecast to see temperatures drop beneath the heatwave threshold for the first time in 21 consecutive days.

Temperatures will largely be in the mid-20s Celsius for the south-east of the UK and in the mid-teens Celsius further north.

For many, the relief from the heat will be short-lived as high pressure is set to build close to the south of the UK next week.

This will stall rain-bearing weather fronts and any wet weather will become confined to northern and western areas - especially north-west Scotland.

In southern parts of the UK, temperatures look set to climb once again.

Tapping into the heat over the near continent, the UK is likely to enter another heatwave, with temperatures in England and Wales forecast to peak around 25-32C for much of next week.

Yellow heat health alerts will come into effect for Yorkshire and Humber, the West and East Midlands, the East of England, London, south-east and south-west, at 9:00 BST on 28 July 2026 and last until 9:00 BST on 31 July.

The UKHSA warns that heat is expected to cause minor impacts for health and social care services, with an increased risk to life for vulnerable people.

News.title: Man charged with two attempted rapes
News.content:
A man has been charged with two counts of attempted rape in Rochdale.

Harvey Symes, 23, is due to appear before Manchester and Salford Magistrates' Court on Monday, Greater Manchester Police said.

The force added that he has also been charged with threats to kill.

It follows an investigation after two women reported being attacked in Broadfield Park and Milnrow Park in the town on Saturday morning.

News.title: My entire family went on a boat trip that they never returned from
News.content:
"It's something you don't get over - you learn to live with it."

Sixty years ago, Peter Watts' entire family was killed in a boating tragedy that shocked the nation.

His nine-year-old sister Angela, 10-year-old brother David, mother Doreen and father Frederick George, along with 11 others, died when the Prince of Wales pleasure boat sank on the Mawddach Estuary in Gwynedd on 22 July, 1966.

Now, a memorial recalling the names of the 15 people who lost their lives has been unveiled.

It was another chance for Peter to travel from the village he grew up in, near Milton Keynes, to the picturesque estuary where the catastrophe unfolded.

News.title: Influencer killed by husband after she accused him of being pedophile on TikTok, police say
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

A social media influencer was shot and killed by her estranged husband after she made a TikTok video accusing him of being a pedophile, according to a police report.

Sara Gilson was killed on Thursday at her home in Owasso, Oklahoma, by her husband, Jeremiah Duffey, whose social media handle was "Shawn Duffey," according to local police.

On June 10, Gilson filed paperwork to secure an emergency protective order against her husband. She made the request a day after police told her that her husband had been accused of molesting a child.

The day before, and approximately a month before Gilson's video, the mother of a 15-year-old girl who played on a basketball team Duffey coached made a police report accusing him of "kissing and fondling her" during a youth basketball event, The Oklahoman reports.

Another coach witnessed the incident, intervened, and informed the girl's parents of what happened.

open image in gallery Influencer Sara Gilson in a TikTok video she made accusing her husband, Jeremiah "Shawn" Duffey, of being a pedophile. Duffey shot and killed Gilson on July 23, approximately two weeks after she posted the video ( Sara Gilson/TikTok )

“Similar conduct by this coach towards this particular juvenile player was reported to have occurred over an extended period of time, in multiple law enforcement jurisdictions, across multiple states prior to this incident,” police said in a statement.

The girl reportedly told her mother that Duffey had sent her inappropriate texts, had invited her to stay with him in his hotel room during a tournament trip, and had offered her money to "keep her quiet" about everything, according to the paper.

Duffey reportedly threatened to kill himself and went into hiding after the incident, according to Gilson's protective custody order.

The day after Gilson was told about the allegations against her husband, she made a TikTok video in which she refers to her "soon to be ex-husband" as a pedophile.

“Preparing for when Netflix drops a documentary about my soon to be ex husband who I just found out is a pedophile,” Gilson wrote in a video caption.

The video — which follows a social media trend of people "preparing" for documentaries focused on strange events in their lives — went viral and has been viewed nearly 18 million times.

“I wish I was joking. #plottwist #netflix #documentary," she wrote in a caption.

Thirteen days after she posted the video, Duffey showed up at her house with a gun.

On Thursday night, a 911 dispatcher received a call from Gilson's address in Collinsville in which a woman was heard screaming and "what sounded to be a gunshot," police said. Dispatchers tried to call back, but the call was not answered.

open image in gallery Jeremiah 'Shawn' Duffey shot and killed his wife, Sara Gilson, and himself on July 23, almost two weeks after Gilson posted a video accusing him of being a pedophile. A 15-year-old girl on Duffey's basketball team accused him of touching her inappropriately during a youth basketball event ( Jeremiah Duffey/TikTok )

Another 911 call was made moments later from a neighbor's house claiming that his stepfather had shot his mother, police said.

When officers arrived at the house, they found both Gilson and Duffey dead from gunshot wounds to the head.

Though the incident is still under investigation, police said it appears to have been a murder-suicide.

Gilson's son was taken into protective custody and released to a parent who was not involved in the incident, police said. Gilson also had a daughter, but it is unclear if she is an adult or if she was released into custody of the same parent.

Andy Burnham will host Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday as his first international visitor since becoming Prime Minister.

The new PM said UK support for Ukraine “remains unwavering” ahead of the visit on Monday, just a week after entering Downing Street.

They will visit a naval base where Mr Burnham will announce that Britain will hand over the intellectual property behind its new “Stone Cloak” electronic warfare system, enabling Ukraine to produce the technology at scale.

The tablet-sized device is designed to block Russian detection of any drones it is fitted to.

The Ministry of Defence has already given thousands of the jammers to Ukrainian forces to bolster their drone operations.

open image in gallery A firefighter walks at the site of a petrol station hit by a Russian airstrike, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in Zaporizhzhia ( Reuters )

Mr Burnham said in a statement: “Britain stands with Ukraine, shoulder to shoulder, and our support remains unwavering.

“Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve and we will not back down until we achieve long-lasting and just peace for Ukraine.

“Stone Cloak is the best of homegrown British innovation and proven on the frontline, and it will be vital to protecting our security in both our countries.”

What is ‘Stone Cloak’?

Following its deployment in Ukraine, the technology is expected to be incorporated into the UK’s next generation of long-range strike weapons, including Project Brakestop, the Government’s initiative to develop low-cost cruise missiles.

During the visit, the two leaders will meet more than 200 Ukrainian military personnel who have spent the past three weeks in the UK taking part in Exercise Sea Breeze, aimed at strengthening warfighting capabilities and counter-mine measures in the Black Sea.

The new Prime Minister spoke to Mr Zelensky in one of his first calls after taking office last Monday and invited the Ukrainian leader to visit “at the earliest opportunity”.

Mr Burnham, who has little foreign policy experience from his previous time in government, had vowed to maintain his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer’s resolute support for Ukraine before entering No 10.

Sir Keir visited Kyiv on his final full day as Labour leader.

open image in gallery Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky pay their respects at a wreath laying at the Wall of Remembrance of the Fallen for Ukraine (Stefan Rousseau/PA) ( PA Wire )

On Sunday Romania shot down a suspected Russian drone after it crossed into its airspace — the third such incursion in three days in the Eastern European nation that's both a European Union and a NATO member, the country's president said.

Two Romanian F-16 fighter jets scrambled from the Fete*ti airbase, under NATO's operational command, and shot down the drone over the Black Sea, the military alliance said.

"A new drone was shot down this morning, at 10:13, by an F-16 aircraft of the Romanian Air Force, over the territorial waters of Romania, in the Sulina-Chilia area," Romanian President Nicusor Dan said.

He added that authorities found that one of the earlier intercepted drones appears to be "a Shahed type, used by the Russian Federation in the war of aggression against Ukraine.

"This is the fourth recent downing by Romania of a drone violating NATO airspace in coordination with the alliance, said Col. Martin O'Donnell, a spokesperson for NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, known as SHAPE.Before the last three interceptions, Romanian jets shot down a drone in the sky above Estonia in May, he said.

Romanian pilots and planes are based in Lithuania from where they have broad strike capabilities as part of NATO's force posture.

"As we continue to prove, NATO is constantly on the watch and prepared to defend itself from any threat," O'Donnell said.

Luke Littler warned he can still get better after crushing Gerwyn Price 18-9 to retain his Betfred World Matchplay title in Blackpool.

Littler was in imperious form as he set a new record for the final with an average of 111.53, lifting his average for the tournament as a whole to 111.04 to break Phil Taylor’s previous high mark of 106.31.

Littler also broke his own competition record for 180s as he hit 12 in the final to reach 66 for the week.

The win keeps Littler on course for a clean sweep of trophies in 2026 having already won the World Championship, UK Open, Premier League and the Masters.

But while the 19-year-old said this was the best version of himself to date, there is still plenty more to come.

“I can still get better,” Littler said. “I can get a lot better. Through the matches, I was up to a 120 average at one point and I didn’t make it stick. Maybe in a few years’ time I will stick it and go up to a 120 average.

“At the minute I’m playing some of the best stuff and I’ve just got to keep it there…

“The main goal was to win every major once. I don’t know how many years are left in me. We’re still only two and a half years into my professional career. It’s far from done.”

Littler suggested his relentless scoring reflected his deep desire to become only the third man to successfully defend the Matchplay title after Taylor and Michael van Gerwen, who achieved it 10 years ago.

“I’ve come out with the best outcome there is in any tournament by lifting the trophy, but the way I’ve done it, I’ve definitely surprised myself but it’s down to the commitment I’ve got.

“I wanted to win this trophy more than anything, go back to back, put my name on that list and that’s what I’ve done. I wasn’t playing the best (in the World Series) but I’ve come here with a different mindset.”

Price, appearing in his first final since 2022 having never won the trophy, had said earlier in the week that if he brought his best to the final he could beat Littler, but it was not the case as, even averaging 104.97, the Welshman was blown away.

“Luke is one in a million,” Price said. “I think I played pretty decent.

“In that game I missed a couple of opportunities but the bull checkouts, the 167, it was a big turning point even though it was early in the game.

open image in gallery Gerwyn Price (right) recognises Littler as “one in a million” (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

“I didn’t play brilliant, but I played decent.”

Earlier Beau Greaves claimed her third Women’s World Matchplay title in four years as she edged out Fallon Sherrock 6-5, taking the win with a checkout of 56 in the deciding leg.

“I’m not one to celebrate but it was relief in the end,” Greaves said. “Fallon is a great lass and an even better darts player. I knew I had to play well but to hit that last dart was an outpouring of relief.”

Elvira Menéndez knows how lucky she.

Her house is not a charred ruin like so many others in Spain and France hit by recent deadly wildfires.

But the 79-year-old retiree can’t help but worry for another family that, like her, fled the raging inferno.

“They have been left with nothing,” said about a young family that lives down her son’s street. “The house has completely burned down, and they have three children.”

The wildfires that have raged out of control in recent days in three provinces in central Spain have ravaged tens of thousands of hectares and forced nearly 90,000 people to flee their homes. In the southwest of France, more than 250,000 people have fled their homes as the fire rages through the wine region of Bordeaux.

open image in gallery Spain Wildfires ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

For the hundreds of thousands of people in this situation, the question is the same: What will they find when they’re finally allowed to go home, or to what’s left of it?

With no word on when she’ll be able to return to Chapinería, her hometown west of the Spanish capital of Madrid, Menéndez will spend her third night on Sunday at the makeshift shelter set up in a sports complex in Villaviciosa de Odón, a 40-minute drive from the home she was forced to leave as the blaze neared.

“At least we’re all together,” said Menéndez, who is at the shelter with her family and their dog.

open image in gallery FireMap reveals where fire has spread near Madrid ( FireMap )

On Friday afternoon, two major fires near Madrid merged into a single, rapidly spreading blaze. It later combined with another that was already burning in Ávila, north of the capital. This forced the government to declare a national fire emergency for the first time. Since then, the flames have also spread to Toledo, a province southwest. In all, the flames have scorched 77,000 hectares in the central part of the country alone.

Menéndez’s anguish was shared by Rocío Domínguez, who fled her house with only the clothes on her back. “All the clothes, all the memories, everything, everything, everything,” were left behind, she told The Associated Press.

“The only thing I had time to grab was a kit I have for the dogs,” Domínguez added, surrounded by her two beloved pets. Everything else she has with her now — from the clothes she wears to her food and toiletries — she received at the shelter.

open image in gallery Spain Wildfires ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

At the evacuation center, where cots have been set up for about 200 people, Domínguez still has the terrifying memory of their escape fresh in her mind.

“It was madness with cars going up and down, traffic jams in the village streets as people tried to get out. It looked like the apocalypse,” told Domínguez, 35 years old and unemployed, who is with her parents and siblings. “You couldn’t see anything.”

“Everything was covered in ash,” she added. “You could see all the burned animals.”

Spanish King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia heard more of those personal testimonies on Sunday as the royals visited another shelter in Villamartín, about 45 kilometers west of Madrid.

And those stories may not be the last — Spain's Minister of Ecological Transition, Sara Aagesen, later noted that “more evacuations are still expected” in that area.

Queen Letizia told reporters after meeting with the survivors that it was important "to hear how they feel and how they recount their hasty departure from their home. How they have felt the sadness they describe, the anguish, the uncertainty, and those questions they leave hanging in the air,.

Wildfire brought tragedy on the heels of Spain's World Cup

The wildfires have significantly shifted the mood in the country, where just a week ago huge crowds of people took to the streets to celebrate their second FIFA World Cup triumph.

As the echoes of those celebrations fade, head coach Luis de la Fuente — one of the driving forces behind the historic victory over Argentina in the final in New Jersey — visited those affected by the fires at a sports center in Las Rozas.

open image in gallery Spain Wildfires ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

The Spanish Football Federation, which has its headquarters in the same city, has offered the facilities where the newly crowned world champions usually train for the vulnerable families who have been forced to evacuate from their homes.

The coach said all of Spain is rallying for the wildfire survivors.

“All of Spain is watching over them,” De la Fuente said in remarks to the national public broadcaster, TVE. “They have the support of the entire country, the same support we have when we play soccer. It’s exactly the same.”

News.title: Four Good Samaritans shot while trying to break up a fight between a man and woman in San Francisco

Four men were shot while trying to break up a fight between a man and a woman in San Francisco on Saturday, police said.

The shooting happened just before 1 a.m. on the corner of Mason and Market streets in the city’s downtown Tenderloin District, San Francisco police told SFGate.

The men who were shot were trying to intervene in an altercation between a man and woman, both of whom were strangers to them.

As the group of good Samaritans tried to stop the pair from arguing, the man pulled out a firearm and shot them, police said.

All four of the men were hospitalized with injuries, but are expected to survive. Authorities did not share the extent of their injuries or any other information about the victims.

open image in gallery Four men were shot while trying to intervene in an altercation between a man and woman in San Francisco ( Getty )

Meanwhile, the shooter fled the scene, and authorities had not located him as of Sunday.

Bilal Mahmood, the supervisor of San Francisco’s District 5, which covers the neighborhood where the shooting unfolded, said on X Saturday that suspects had been identified, but no arrests were made yet.

“I was present at the crime scene and spoke to officers on the scene,” Mahmood wrote. “Thanks to the actions of SFPD and RTIC, suspects have been identified.”

“We appreciate the swift actions of our first responders, and will be monitoring the situation as it develops,” he added.

Authorities did not specify what the man and woman were arguing about when the incident unfolded.

News.content:

Americans are not buying Donald Trump’s predictions that the Iran war is nearing its end, nor do they believe that Iran has lost the will or the means to keep fighting.

And one of his top advisers is no longer sticking to that timeline, either.

U.N. Ambassador Mike Waltz appeared on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday and unlike other senior Trump administration officials who’ve appeared on the Sunday circuit previously, the ambassador would not commit to the war ending before the end of 2026.

"I'm not going to put some kind of timeline on it,” said Waltz.

His comments come as the president has dismissed the idea of further negotiatons and allowed the war to resume at full strength after a 60-day extension of the ceasefire between the two countries dissolved earlier this month. A tanker struck a mine in the Strait of Hormuz and exploded this weekend as the crucial waterway has become increasingly unsafe, once again, for global shipping traffic.

open image in gallery U.N. Ambassador Mike Waltz defended Trump's war with Iran on NBC on Sunday ( NBC - Meet the Press )

They reveal a growing sense of doubt within the administration itself, with fewer and fewer officials willing to say that the war is definitively over amid a withering barrage of criticism from Capitol Hill. Though senators continue to defeat War Powers resolutions aimed at restricting the president’s power, the Senate GOP caucus is increasingly opposed to the war and several senators have spoken out about their beliefs that the war was a mistake from the beginning.

Elsewhere on Sunday a new poll revealed that Americans have abandoned the Trump administration as a reliable source of information about the topic of Iran. A CBS News poll found that only a single digit percentage of Americans now believe the White House’s predictions — that the war will be over within days, or a couple weeks.

open image in gallery Vessels transiting through the Gulf of Oman are pictured off the coast of Muscat ( AFP/Getty )

Instead, more than half believe the opposite — that the war will likely continue for many months or even years, as the conflict approaches the five-month mark and senior Trump officials appear unable to break a deadlock in the negotiations, which are now on the backburner altogether thanks to the resumption of hostilities. This week, the president attended the dignified transfer of four U.S. service members killed in an Iranian attack this month, and claimed afterwards without any proof that the slain soldiers “said very strongly” that “we can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon”.

Waltz, in his interview, dodged a question from Kristen Welker on whether Americans should brace for further casualties.

The ceasefire extension signed by Trump in June agreed to the principle of beginning negotiations over Iran’s nuclear material, but significant differences remain over the U.S. and Iranian positions over the future of Iran’s nuclear energy ambitions.

open image in gallery 'They said, and all of them said very strongly, 'We can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon,' President Trump said of US service members who died in the Iran war ( AFP/Getty )

The war itself remains highly unpopular, and has been blamed by a Koch-linked group in a new statement for detracting from GOP voter enthusiasm as the midterms approach. Gas prices passed $4 a gallon nationally for the second time this year in July, spurred by new hostilities in the Strait of Hormuz and the breakdown of talks between the U.S. and Iran, and the associated costs of transporting goods have begun to spread out into other sectors of consumer goods.

The problem is particularly of issue to Republicans as the president ran and won on an economic message in 2024 which, in part, stressed that he would avoid entering “forever” wars in the Middle East and elsewhere that he correctly blamed for driving up prices.

Republicans are now faced with a midterm electorate suffering a sense of betrayal over the president’s campaign promises, a problem that polling shows extends to core members of Donald Trump’s Republican base as well.

U.S. and Iranian forces have paused attacks in the region for the past two days, with the exact reasons unclear. A White House spokesperson indicated that diplomatic talks remained Trump’s preferred outcome, but the existence or scope of any talks have not yet been confirmed.

“President Trump has always been consistent in saying he prefers a diplomatic solution, but he continues to retain all options if Iran continues terrorist activities in the Strait of Hormuz or against allies," White House spokesman Steven Cheung said.

“It’s been a crazy week, one of the best weeks of my life with the darts I’ve played,” Littler said. “It’s not been easy, it’s been tough.

“The stats make it look easy but when you’re on this stage with how hot it is, I’ve definitely played some of the best darts of my life.

“I feel like it’s the best version of myself. I have just played so well.”

Littler is eyeing a clean sweep of the majors, and will now turn his attention to the Pro Tour in order to qualify for the Player Championship Finals.

“I don’t think my dad is too happy because we were meant to be going to Spain but now we will be going to Leicester for some Pro Tours!” he said.

News.title: Lando Norris comes in from the cold with dominant Hungarian GP victory
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix from the Hungaroring. This is the 40th anniversary of the race at this track and the 41st edition. I think over the years this track has had a bit of an unfair reputation but we have certainly had some interesting and exciting races over the years. Even over the last few years.

The nature of the track means it is a bit of an outlier. And that means you often get results that go away from the norm of the season. Mercedes took a couple of poles here in the ground-effect era whilst Charles Leclerc did so last year. We have had a handful of first-time winners at this track, too: Damon Hill, Fernando Alonso, Esteban Ocon, Jenson Button and… errr Heikki Kovalainen.

So far that has been true this weekend. Although McLaren and Ferrari have been closing in on Mercedes, the SIlver Arrows have usually had the edge or found it when it comes to qualifying. That was not the case yesterday: Lando Norris took the first non-Mercedes grand prix pole of the season, pipping the Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton by just 0.012sec.

Hamilton, though, takes a three-place grid penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri in Q3. Kimi Antonelli, who had qualified fourth, takes the same penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. It was Ferrari who had been expected to be the team to beat but they were the team that dropped the ball. In fairness Norris, in the upgraded McLaren had looked competitive throughout qualifying and was simply able to deliver when Ferrari could not.

The grid is slightly mixed up because of the penalties. George Russell’s season did not get any easier after qualifying seventh but he at least moves up because of those grid drops. The Mercedes’ race pace is expected to be strong but will it be enough to put them into contention with the McLarens and the Ferraris? And let’s not forget Max Verstappen in fourth, either…

We find out at 2pm BST, when the race gets under way.

News.title: Anthony Joshua knocks out Kristian Prenga after worst round of his career
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Anthony Joshua’s heavyweight clash with Kristian Prenga, taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The kingdom plays host to yet another major boxing event, and this is the second part of a weekend that serves as a build-up to a potentially huge match-up later this year.

Prenga’s 20 wins have come against pedestrian opposition, and if he wins tonight then it would be such an upset as to probably finish Joshua’s career as a real name in the sport.

Joshua, the former unified champion, has plenty of defeats to his name. Oleksandr Usyk, twice, as well as Daniel Dubois and Andy Ruiz Jnr.

Tonight should show us where he is. After his loss to Dubois in 2024 he did not fight again until December 2025, when he rearranged Jake Paul’s ability first to stand up, and second, to chew.

A win for Joshua tonight means that all eyes turn to the end of the year, when he is expected to finally meet Tyson Fury in the ring to settle their rivalry.

Now both are deposed champions, the interest has waned a tad, but it remains the biggest all-British clash that anybody could conceive.

Fury, for his part, had little trouble against Mariusz Wach last night, the 46-year-old journeyman who he fought in Thailand. While that was not broadcast live, the clips online hardly suggested it was a classic, but it was enough to keep Fury active as he maintained his focus and avoided his own banana skin.

Joshua now needs to show that he is capable of finishing a fight. If he struggles, he invites pressure for the next four or five months in the build-up to meeting Fury.
