Sports.title: Teamwork, tactics and data: behind the scenes at Wigan’s pre-season training
Sports.content:
“This is the only rule I’m going to have for yous all season: ‘team first’,” says Gary Caldwell. The Wigan head coach’s Scottish accent booms over the gentle hum of a projector in a darkened classroom at the club’s Christopher Park training ground. “That is the one thing that we cannot ever go against,” he says, pointing to a slide on screen. “The team is the most important aspect of everything we do.”

Three rows of professional athletes listen intently, keen to learn not only what the day holds, but about the 10 months ahead.

Some shall see it through to next May, others may leave before the 2026-27 League One campaign begins on 14 August, and new faces will be added.

It is pre-season and before the interminable football carousel begins spinning, there is much work ahead.

View image in fullscreen Gary Caldwell talks tactics with his squad. Photograph: Dom Maltby/The Guardian

The meeting is short, just long enough for Caldwell to zip through a handful of tactical points. As he speaks, the head of performance analysis, Lauren Jones, plays clips from their “best practice bank”.

Because she, Caldwell, and the first-team coach, David Perkins, joined from Exeter only in February (the physio, Michael McBride, and goalkeeping coach, Kevin Miller, followed this summer), the bank is small, but growing.

There are myriad general football clips that Caldwell could use, but he values “the lads seeing players in Wigan shirts doing what we’re asking of them”.

Perkins relays the day’s plan – a 1.5km time trial, several drills, some out-of-possession shape work and an afternoon weights session – before the class is dismissed and told to reassemble on the grass 45 minutes later.

There is no idling, though, the entire squad soon beginning self‑led pre-activation (in old money, warming up).

Bodies are strewn across the in-house gym with bands, benches and foam rollers used as aids to contort muscles and limbs.

Wigan’s facility is, by modern standards, modest but functional. A printed sign sets out the simple rules: £50 fines for anyone with a phone, wearing sliders or sulking.

When the centre-back James Carragher discovers the Guardian will be joining the morning’s run, a sanction of double that amount is declared should anyone not beat the guest journalist. At 10.55am, the strength and conditioning lead, Matthew Barrow, explains that the run consists of 15 pitch lengths with 14 turns. “Your choice lads – boots or trainers, but I recommend boots so you don’t lose time on the turn.”

“I’m glad I’m not doing it,” Caldwell says, laughing. “It’s a maximal test and anything like that involves people pushing themselves.”

Could you survive a professional football pre-season fitness test? – video

It is not the squad’s first testing of pre-season. Their first day back involved a series of body and strength tests “designed to provide us with a benchmark”, Caldwell says. “If they get injured, we know where we need to get them back to.”

But the days of players reporting back overweight are long gone, with only a small number a smidge above their optimum numbers during body composition testing. “That will all have been gone with the first week or so,” Caldwell says.

Running for running’s sake is also past practice. Instead, Barrow and the sports scientist Jack Craigie will use the run data to get each individual’s maximum aerobic speed. “From that, we individualise all the running they’ll do,” Craigie says. “For example, if we have a volume session planned, rather than giving a generic number of lengths, we set individual distances based on their results. That way they all get the same stimulus.”

By 11am, the players are jogging through a warm-up lap. According to the sign-in sheet outside the staff offices, some arrived on site three hours ago. The physio hub just off the gym has had a steady stream of visitors, a mix of prevention and cure. Breakfast was enjoyed in a canteen acting as a social space for staff and players.

It marks a leisurely start when measured against some mornings. With no tour plans, Caldwell is finding alternative ways to avoid monotony. Several 6am meets precede 3.5km runs to a partner gym for intense, Hyrox-style workouts. With players working in trios, staff are as interested in attitude and demeanour as fitness.

View image in fullscreen The players take part in various training drills. Photograph: Dom Maltby/The Guardian

“We’re taking the group out of their comfort zone to see how they react under a bit of pressure,” Caldwell says. “We can look at the energy someone brings at 6am when others are tired. That will help us know who is going to pick the group up when we’re a little fatigued.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Those sessions also promote Caldwell’s “team first” ethos. “When you’re ‘off’ you still have a role to play,” he says. “Are you helping your pal get in and out of the straps on the rower more quickly? We want to see how they react in that situation. Come November, when it is cold and we’re struggling in a game, we can remind them of these sessions.”

A late-morning run feels tame by comparison, albeit after several pitch lengths that naive notion is dispelled. No one loses £100 to the club kitty.

Soon the footballs are out and the group is split into two groups for a series of drills. The energy is impressive, with Max Power, who recently rejoined Wigan for a third spell, among the tone setters.

In one exercise he encourages a junior teammate to make a pass, only for a defender to block the space. Rather than get frustrated or dish out abuse, Power immediately finds another opportunity to tee up a similar ball and praises a successful outcome. “The better the player, the less stick they give people, I find,” says one staff member. “They want everyone to improve.”

The staff’s challenge is to manage the intensity, building towards a peak. Caldwell avoids directly asking players to hold back, but with a drone monitoring everything and GPS data available in real time, sessions can be adjusted accordingly. Sometimes it is as simple as moving cones in a few yards.

For one drill, tape on the grass creates a dozen boxes, within which three banks of four must work to create and find gaps. “Football is sometimes about the chaos,” Caldwell says, grinning. “If we give them more space, they will use it.”

View image in fullscreen Wigan use the in-house gym during a break from the action on the pitch. Photograph: Dom Maltby/The Guardian

Building towards a peak is also Wigan’s aim. Supporters want a return to the relatively recent success, which is natural after eight seasons as an established Premier League side. That ended in 2013 – the year they lifted the FA Cup at Wembley with Caldwell in the squad.

Four Championship relegations and three League One promotions have followed, including in Caldwell’s first full season in management. That was 2015-16 and the third-tier title was claimed.

Caldwell’s immediate challenge last season was avoiding relegation from League One, and patience is required for the next step.

After lunch, the day concludes in the gym with a short, sharp, upper body strength session. In one corner, pull-ups, in another perfectly formed jackknives.

“Once the season begins, training loads are consistent around games,” Barrow says. “But with the time in here now we can really chase that hypertrophy.”

Pre-season was once, in effect, punishment for a summer well enjoyed, but in 2026 is a meticulous, data-driven, foundation-building exercise.

The payoff will become known only next May.

Sports.title: Chiesa wants ‘new chapter’ with Iraola after frustrating time under Slot at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Federico Chiesa has said he wants “a new chapter” at Liverpool with Andoni Iraola following a frustrating time under Arne Slot and claimed the club were lucky to qualify for the Champions League last season.

The Liverpool forward has been linked with a return to Italy this summer having struggled for minutes during his two years at Anfield. Chiesa made 36 appearances for Slot last season, a healthy return on paper, but only five were starts.

He started one Premier League game last season despite the problems Liverpool had in attack because of injuries to Alexander Isak and Hugo Ekitiké, and his last start came in the FA Cup fourth-round win against Brighton on 14 February. A change of head coach, Chiesa hopes, will herald a change in fortune as a Liverpool player.

“It is always a fresh start at the beginning of the year,” said the 28-year-old, who produced a fine finish in Liverpool’s 4-2 friendly defeat of Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday. “Maybe there have been too many fresh starts [for him]. But I don’t care, I am trying to do my best for this new manager.

“Last season under Arne Slot, I was trying to do my best. Last year I felt ready for a bigger role, then it depended on the coach whether he wanted me to play or not. Of course I wanted to play more but it is what it is. The gaffer had his gameplans, he took his decisions, I have nothing to say about that. It is football. This year, let us say it is a new chapter. There is a new manager and I have to focus on that.”

Chiesa admits he has not discussed his future with Iraola since the Basque coach succeeded Slot in June. “The only conversations I had were about pressing and tactics,” he said. “He put me striker against Sunderland and he wants me there.”

But the Italy international, who has two years remaining on his Liverpool contract, claimed his priority is to prove himself to the head coach rather than seek a return to Serie A. Como and former club Juventus have been linked with a move for the forward.

“Right now, at the moment, I am happy here at Liverpool,” said Chiesa. “I love the club, I love the fans, I love everything. I am doing the best I can to have a chance here. And then we will see. At the minute, the only thing I am thinking about is Liverpool.”

View image in fullscreen Federico Chiesa scored for Liverpool against Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday. Photograph: George Walker IV/AP

Liverpool secured Champions League qualification on the final day of a troubled season in May in what proved to be Slot’s final game in charge. Chiesa insists that was no cause for celebration at a club of Liverpool’s stature and there must be improvement next term.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The forward said: “Liverpool deserves more. Two years ago, we were Premier League champions. Last year, we almost went out of the Champions League spots. We were battling for fifth, which was enough at the time but as we know usually only four go in. We were lucky.

“It was a tough season last year and this season we need to do better, in the Champions League as well. We went out to PSG. We want to go further in that competition and then we want to do even better in the Premier League as well.”

Chiesa also hopes to reclaim his place in the national team next season, having missed out on several squads recently. Italy are now searching for a new head coach, having failed to qualify for the World Cup under Gennaro Gattuso.

Chiesa said: “The situation is that I spoke to the manager a few times, Gattuso, and I was not ready physically at the time. When I got back in March, unfortunately I got injured. But I am looking forward to playing for the national team. I have won with the national team [the European Championship]. It is always nice to play and win for your national team.”

Sports.title: Régis Le Bris says Chelsea’s pursuit of Sunderland captain Xhaka is ‘closed’
Sports.content:
Régis Le Bris has declared Chelsea’s pursuit of Granit Xhaka “closed” and insisted there is no prospect of Sunderland selling their influential captain this summer.

Xhaka played a major role in Sunderland qualifying for the Europa League on their return to the Premier League last season, prompting Chelsea to make an £8m bid for the 33-year-old this month. Xabi Alonso, the new Chelsea manager, is keen to be reunited with his former midfielder at Bayer Leverkusen.

Sunderland, however, immediately rejected Chelsea’s bid and their head coach has emphatically denied that a deal could be revisited before the end of the transfer window.

“No, this topic is closed,” said Le Bris after Sunderland’s 4-2 pre-season friendly defeat by Liverpool in Nashville on Saturday. “He has been really clear about his future. He loves Sunderland, he wants to stay in Sunderland. He wants to make the future of Sunderland. He is a good captain. Great leader.”

Despite the added demands of European football next season Sunderland have been quiet in the transfer market, signing only the experienced Belgium defender Thomas Meunier on a free from Lille so far. Le Bris anticipates further additions but admits this summer will be nothing like the rebuilding work before Sunderland’s return to the top flight 12 months ago.

The Sunderland head coach added: “It’s going to be quiet. Under the radar, right? I won’t give you information. Because I think we are working hard behind the scenes, and it’s really important to be quiet because otherwise it’s a mess. And we are looking at probably a different transfer window if you compare with last season. We had to sign 14 new players. It won’t be the case this year. We’ll see what will happen.”

Sports.title: ‘We want to win the league’: Arsenal’s new recruits ink in WSL success
Sports.content:
Georgia Stanway looks at her arms and then down at her legs on day one of Arsenal’s pre-season. “As you can see, I’m covered in tattoos,” she says. “I only see the bare skin, the space, so I need to keep collecting more.”

Tattooing and being tattooed is her creative outlet, her way of expressing herself off the pitch. But seeing space is key to the 27‑year‑old England midfielder being exceptional on the pitch.

Stanway’s unveiling video, after her move from Bayern Munich, showed a delicate, cursive script reading “whatever the weather” tattooed on her arm. It was a bold statement to get the lyric from North London Forever, Arsenal’s anthem, etched into her skin before she has stepped on to the Emirates Stadium pitch in red and white. “It shows I’m going to give absolutely everything for this club. I want to hit the ground running, play my game, connect with my teammates, connect with the fans and look forward to an exciting future at the club.”

Stanway is emblematic of Arsenal’s summer of change, one of seven signings so far. Meanwhile, Lotte Wubben-Moy, a lifelong fan who joined Arsenal’s academy at 13, represents the core and culture that is a point of focus at the club. It is a culture players want to be a part of, so much so it leads to getting a tattoo on day one of being there. “She has set a very high bar,” says Wubben-Moy, with a grin. “That’s Georgia. She goes all in and I like that.”

Wubben-Moy is ready to stake a claim in Arsenal’s starting XI after struggling to nail down a position in defence despite having performed exceptionally well when covering for injured players. “I’ve always felt ready,” says the 27-year-old. “When I get my moment, I deliver. Historically, as a club, we’re built on defensive solidity. If we have a solid defence, it allows us to create and score. That should be the stepping stone towards victories. So I will continue to contribute to the defensive solidity in whatever way, shape or form that is. But I want my spot.”

View image in fullscreen Lotte Wubben-Moy lifts the Champions Cup trophy during the Arsenal trophy parade in May. Photograph: Alex Burstow/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

There was widespread recognition that Arsenal’s squad needed a revamp, that the age needed to be lowered and changes made if they were going to take the next step. That meant big names leaving, most notably Beth Mead and Katie McCabe. “They’re both absolute legends of the game and we have so much respect for them,” says Jodie Taylor, the former Arsenal striker who became the club’s technical director in January. “But we always knew this window was going to come with some changes.”

“Change is inevitable in women’s football,” says Wubben-Moy. “If you speak to a player and they don’t say they’re nimble, you’ve got someone that’s not built for the game. We’ve become a nimble team, a team that can move with the ebb and flow of women’s football.

View image in fullscreen Beth Mead left in a busy summer for Arsenal. Photograph: Rhianna Chadwick/PA

“That’s not just within the playing group, it’s something replicated within the staff, the boardroom, the commercial team, the comms team. Everyone is so willing to move and to dictate what we want.

“If you’d asked me about change four or five years ago, I’d have been a bit intimidated, but now I know what to do and I’m part of the driver of it. The opportunity we have and that I see for us as a team, as a collective, is something that really excites me.”

Arsenal’s approach to Stanway’s recruitment was a contributing factor to her wanting to join the club. “Arsenal came in early doors,” she says. “I really enjoyed they were super loyal from the beginning and wanted me even when I wasn’t available. It’s a nice feeling being wanted.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The last four years in Munich were unbelievable, but I knew I wanted to take the next step and I felt at Arsenal there was an opportunity for me to be able to progress, to make my game better and to play with world-class players.”

Arsenal have done most of their business early, with Stanway joined by experienced internationals Selina Cerci, Géraldine Reuteler, Ona Batlle and Misa Rodríguez, as well as young talents Lisa Baum and Isabella Damm. No major international tournament and seven signings in for day one of pre-season is a big boost for Renée Slegers and her coaching staff, particularly after two seasons of slow starts to domestic campaigns.

“The market is not easy, though, it’s constantly changing and the pool of elite talent is small and several clubs are fishing from it,” says Taylor. “You try and plan as much as you can, but you also have to be reactive in the market. We’re always trying to keep an eye on the future, but we have to be quite agile.

“We can talk about positional needs, qualities, ages and succession planning, but if a player’s not available or they just don’t exist, it can be like trying to fit square pegs and round holes. As well as looking at current needs and positional profiles, we talk a lot about our core style of play, but we also want to play with variety, be unpredictable and have different qualities in players too.”

View image in fullscreen Former Arsenal striker Jodie Taylor, now technical director, is leading the strong recruitment this summer. Photograph: Zuma Press/Alamy

The players who have come in have brought energy, says Wubben-Moy, who was on an emotional rollercoaster during Arsenal men’s Premier League and women’s Champions Cup-winning parade, with the bus looping past Highbury Corner, where she filmed her contract renewal video, and past Islington town hall, where she got married to cyclist Tao Geoghegan Hart a few weeks later.

“I like to focus on what they’re entering,” says Wubben-Moy, “which is a culture that has been created by history, by players and staff that are the core of this team and who have all lived through the changes to different degrees: Kelly [Smith], Renée, myself, Leah [Williamson], Kim [Little], Jodie too. We’ve been privy to lots of different things but all of us are holding on to and releasing, in a healthy way, the things we know we need to. It’s efficient, we’re focused, we know what we do next.

“It’s like you’re cooking the most beautiful recipe and then you add the final small ingredients that make the marginal difference, that elevate, and you create something that’s beautiful and that you can relish and enjoy. That’s what we’re in the process of now with a beautiful long pre-season. I’m desperate to get it out of the way so we can then serve what we’re cooking to the fans and be like: ‘Let’s eat and we’ll all eat together for the whole year.’”

The average attendance of more than 34,000 fans for WSL games at the Emirates last season and the club’s pioneering history in women’s football, as well as the Champions League win in 2025, are huge selling points, and all concerned at Arsenal want more, including a first Women’s Super League title since 2019.

“We’re in a great place,” says Taylor. “But we would have liked to have won more trophies last season and that is our huge ambition coming into this year. I’ll flat out say it: we want to win the league. We are an ambitious club and with the signings we’ve made we feel like we’re in a great place to do that.”

Sports.title: How the death of Jayden Adams shook a community: ‘Being on the pitch was his happy place’
Sports.content:
For Jayden Adams, the South Africa midfielder who died this month at the age of 25, football was a “safe space”. Those words, used by Adams’s junior coach Steve Barker at his memorial service 10 days ago, tell you everything you need to know about his life beyond the pitch.

Adams’s battles were bestowed on him almost from birth. Though he was born into newly democratic South Africa, by the early 2000s the revolution was well on its way to being betrayed. The vote was extended to all, but few could make full use of the freedoms available to them because socioeconomic circumstances in the country had barely changed. Stellenbosch, where the Adams family were based, is a perfect example.

Its facade is a tourist dream: a university town nestled among vineyards, Cape Dutch architecture and indie boutiques. Most visitors never venture beyond the town centre or into its suburbs, which are home to the far less privileged and are havens of neglect. Those areas are classic apartheid hangovers, where the wealth has been preserved for a historically advantaged elite and those on the margins, working-class communities of people of colour, are all but invisible.

Ironically, that is how Adams is most often described. He moved in the shadows, both of society and the sport in which he excelled. “Jayden was a guy of very few words. He was quiet, very shy and the smallest among his teammates,” Brendine Johnson, an Adams family spokesperson, says. “Initially, a lot of people missed his football qualities because of his size, but he had a very good fighting spirit. It just wasn’t always on display.”

Adams loved the game dearly and his aunt Monica Thaoge recalled how, as a child, he would kick anything round – “even onions” she said at his memorial. His parents, Juanito and Candice, previously mentioned potatoes as their son’s football of choice. Nobody in the family talks about lacking in financial means because theirs was a community striving to make life better. But there were absences, especially early on.

View image in fullscreen Members of the Mamelodi Sundowns football club carry Jayden Adams’ coffin at the funeral service for the player on Saturday. Photograph: Esa Alexander/Reuters

“Everybody in areas like that is just trying to make ends meet,” says Roger Telemachus, the former South Africa cricketer who grew up on the same street as Adams’s father in Cloetesville. “For the kids, they may not have noticed so much because they were occupied, mostly with playing sport. Some fathers, like Juanito, really encouraged their kids and everyone used to play everything on the street: tennis, football, rugby, cricket. It was also the best way of staying out of trouble.”

Problems were there for everyone to see and, according to Telemachus, have got worse “in the last 20 years”. They include gangsterism, substance abuse and crimes that range from petty to serious. Adams was able to escape from that life when he moved to the slightly more affluent area of Ida’s Valley, but still he did not have a life of luxury. For a period, the family of six, which included four children, lived in a two-bedroom place. At other times, they were with his maternal grandmother, Marianna. “He basically grew up in her yard,” says Johnson.

Things started to change for Adams when he was picked for the Stellenbosch Academy Under-18 side at the age of 15. “The environment was tough, especially if you are not big or tall enough, but when physicality was no longer the most important thing, people saw that Jayden was technically very good,” says Johnson.

His coaches agree. Barker, the nephew of South Africa’s Afcon winning coach, Clive, and the current coach of Simba in Tanzania, gave an emotional assessment of Adams’s skills shortly after his death. “You get many good footballers but you get few great footballers. Jayden was great,” he told Newzroom Afrika.

“Jayden had three attributes that set him apart: an incredible first touch, his weight of pass – I’ve never seen anything like it – and he loved the game so much. Being on the pitch was his happy place. He didn’t pass the ball, he used to caress the ball. He was special and his football intelligence was just outstanding.”

View image in fullscreen Jayden Adams played in South Africa’s World Cup group game against Czechia despite the death of his grandmother the day before. Photograph: Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images

It was under Barker that Adams blossomed. He became the first player from the Stellenbosch Academy to play in South Africa’s top flight, the Premier Soccer League. Five years and an international call up later, the country’s richest club, Mamelodi Sundowns, came calling. This year, at the start of his second season with them, Adams shaved his head, in what he joked was a sign of maturity and called himself a “grootman” (big man). The nickname stuck.

Adams never said it, but he may also have realised how much he had grown up. By then, he had been picked, played for and dropped from the national side after arriving late at a training camp and irking the head coach, Hugo Broos. He had also lost two of his academy teammates, including a close friend.

In February 2023, Oshwin Andries, who was 19, died from stabbing injuries he sustained in Paarl, which is 16km north of Stellenbosch. Three years later, Jeandre Gaffoor, 20, drowned in the Krom River.

When Sundowns won the CAF Champions League in May, Adams dedicated his medal to Andries. To lose so much has weighed on the town, but through Adams they have had reason to celebrate.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Fortnightly Sign up to The Hotspot A new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisis Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Members of Adams’s family, including his father, Juanito (centre left), and mother, Candice (centre right), at his memorial service last week. Photograph: Rodger Bosch/AFP/Getty Images

His role in Sundowns’ continental victory and a call-up to the World Cup squad suggested Adams’s career trajectory was rising. After a first season at Sundowns when he was often playing off the bench and his place in the side was questioned, he had become integral to the team. At Adams’s memorial, the Sundowns senior coach, Steve Komphela, called him “the heart of our team and the heartbeat of our playing style” who “understood the game like a coach and played it as a player”.

In the past year, Adams was playing to the potential people who knew him well had seen years ago and surprising others with his courage and drive to succeed. South Africa’s captain, Ronwen Williams, recalled an incident at this year’s Africa Cup of Nations when the tiny Adams took on a tall Mali opponent with some choice local words. Williams asked Adams if he knew the size of the player he was sledging, but Adams shrugged it off and replied that the Malian wouldn’t understand anyway.

“That was the character he had,” Williams said at the memorial, smiling through his tears as he bade farewell to the teammate he called “my ma se kind” (my mother’s child, a term of endearment used in South Africa).

As his star rose, Adams was careful not to advertise his achievements. “Jayden knew what he had, but he never wanted to voice it. He was very competitive, but he would never brag,” says Johnson. “You get people who are very good verbally on social media. Jayden was not like that. And he wanted to give back. After every game, he would be giving away shirts and boots to kids who asked.”

He also concentrated on providing for his family because he “always promised them he would change their financial situation”.

View image in fullscreen Jayden Adams signs a South Africa shirt for a young Mexican fan who arrived at the team’s World Cup hotel. ‘He wanted to give back.’ Photograph: SAFA

At the World Cup, Adams played for them, even through immense pain. His grandmother Marianna died the day before South Africa’s match against Czechia and Adams opted to remain with the squad. He played that match and appeared in good spirits afterwards and called the 1-1 draw positive, even if he was feeling the opposite way.

He also played the next game against South Korea, which South Africa won to reach the knockouts for the first time. Post-game footage showed him sitting on his own while the rest of the squad celebrated with a signature song and dance.

At the memorial, Komphela offered the Adams family a Bible verse as a comfort, but it may as well be a summary. Psalm 23:4: “Though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me.”

They will know Adams took that walk many times over his short life and he did not fear. He leaves behind his parents, three siblings, a partner, two children and a community who have gone through what no neighbourhood should. In all that, he has gone from not wanting to be known, to entering the footballing world’s spotlight. A minute’s silence was observed at several World Cup games in Adams’s memory. That is not the way his family would have pictured him coming to global attention, but it has shown them that, in football, he was always far more valued than anyone thought.

“I don’t think the community knew how big he was and how people enjoyed his football,” says Johnson. “It’s a huge shock.”

Sports.title: Inter enter talks with Tottenham over signing captain Cristian Romero
Sports.content:
Inter have entered talks with Tottenham over the potential signing of Cristian Romero. The Spurs captain helped Argentina reach a second straight World Cup final this month, but could leave this summer for a significant fee after an eventful five-year spell.

The centre-back has made 156 appearances since he joined Tottenham in 2021 and guided the club to Europa League success last year, but served four separate suspensions during a difficult 2025-26 campaign.

With Jan Paul van Hecke signed for £52m from Brighton and Marcos Senesi joining as a free agent in June to boost the defensive options of Roberto De Zerbi’s side, Spurs will let Romero depart and his representatives have been in Milan for talks with Inter this weekend.

Inter’s sporting director, Piero Ausilio, told Sky Italy: “It’s definitely a deal we are trying to sign with the player and the club. These things take some time but there’s definitely interest. Let’s see.”

Sports.title: Japan football great ‘King Kazu’ Miura, 59, scores first competitive goal in four years
Sports.content:
The Japanese football legend Kazuyoshi Miura scored his first competitive goal ⁠in nearly four years on Saturday, finding the net at the age of ⁠59 as ⁠Fukushima ​United thrashed Iwaki Furukawa 7-0 to advance in the Emperor’s Cup.

Miura, affectionately known ⁠as King Kazu, struck in the 52nd minute to put Fukushima 5-0 ahead, capping a trademark ⁠run into the box by meeting a teammate’s ​cutback with a first-time ‌finish at 59 ‌years and 149 days.

The goal sparked celebrations among teammates ‌on the pitch and the bench before the veteran forward was substituted three minutes later.

It was Miura’s first competitive goal since November 2022, when he scored for Suzuka PG, now Atletico Suzuka, in ‌a Japan Football League defeat by FC Osaka.

The former Japan international is preparing for ​a remarkable 42nd season as a professional after extending his loan spell with third-tier Fukushima United until June 2027.

Miura joined the club from Yokohama FC in ⁠December and will remain with Fukushima after making six ​appearances ​during a shortened 2026 ​campaign.

With Japan’s professional leagues set to switch ​from a ‌spring-to-autumn schedule to ​an ​autumn-to-spring calendar, Miura will enter his 60s next February still playing professionally, adding another chapter to one of football’s most enduring careers.

Sports.title: Tottenham begin tour with victory over Auckland FC in front of record crowd
Sports.content:
Dane Scarlett and Richarlison were on target as an under-strength Tottenham opened their pre-season tour with an entertaining 2-0 win over the A-League champions, Auckland FC, on Sunday.

Roberto De Zerbi rested most of his top players but the Premier League side dominated a match played in damp conditions. The 40,112 who packed into the All Blacks’ famed rugby ground formed the biggest crowd to watch a men’s football match in New Zealand. It surpassed the previous best of 37,034 for a New Zealand World Cup qualifying match against Peru in 2017. They were treated to a fast-paced contest, even if both sides were missing several of their best players.

Tottenham have embarked on an aggressive summer of spending after narrowly avoiding relegation last season, when they finished 17th. However, the only notable new signing to take the field was the former West Ham midfielder Mateus Fernandes, who scored in the 1-0 win over MK Dons in London on Wednesday.

De Zerbi said he would ease others into the tour, with Tottenham to play games in Sydney next week against the A-League side Sydney FC and their London rivals Chelsea.

“It’s a chance for the young players,” De Zerbi told TVNZ before kick-off, declaring Jan Paul van Hecke, signed from Brighton, and the former Liverpool stalwart Andy Robertson not yet up to speed. “After a very long trip, we can’t take a risk with the players who are not ready to play yet.”

The cecord club signing, Sandro Tonali, was not considered because the former Newcastle midfielder had suffered an unspecified injury – “one small problem” – before the team left London, De Zerbi added.

Fernandes came on with half an hour remaining and Spurs bagged their second goal shortly afterwards through the work of two other substitutes. Mathys Tel burst into the box and set up a tap-in for Richarlison.

Scarlett, one of several Spurs academy players in action, opened the scoring in the 12th minute, pouncing after the Auckland goalkeeper Michael Woud parried Manor Solomon’s shot.

Sports.title: Female referee left concussed after being knocked over by brawling men's players during melee in match in France
Sports.content:
A female referee reportedly suffered a concussion after being knocked to the ground during a melee in a men's friendly match in France.

Referee Mathilde Demoncay had taken charge of the friendly between Ligue 2 French side Metz and their Dutch opponents Fortuna Sittard on Sunday.

Demoncay had blown for a free kick to Fortuna Sittard in the 39th minute, after a Metz player had pulled the shirt of a breaking attacker.

The fouled Fortuna Sittard player was then seen squaring up to two Metz players following the incident.

This led to Demoncay racing over in an attempt to break up the incident, while players from both teams also ran in as the melee grew.

Footage showed Demoncay, 26, being knocked over backwards as more players pushed into the melee.

Referee Mathilde Demoncay suffered a concussion after being knocked to the ground during a melee between players during a friendly in France

Demoncay had attempted to intervene in the brawl but was knocked down as more players got involved

One player was seen signalling for medical attention with Demoncay appearing to have hit her head on the ground after falling

While unclear on the footage, Demoncay appeared to hit her head on the ground after falling.

One Fortuna player was quick to notice the stricken referee, as they stood by the official and motioned for medical staff to come to her aid.

Medical staff, assistant referees and security came onto the pitch, with Demoncay receiving assistance.

The footage showed Demoncay sitting up as medical staff began to assess her, while players appeared to have become concerned by the incident.

Demoncay was ultimately unable to continue the match, with one of her assistants forced to step in.

The incident, which played out with a sign in the background reading 'respect the referee', led to two players being booked.

Fortuna Sittard had described it as a 'remarkable moment' on the club's website.

Metz, who had been leading 1-0 at the time, went on to win 3-1 in the friendly.

Sports.title: Liverpool working to complete deal for Bradley Barcola - with France star open to move but PSG demanding £140MILLION
Sports.content:
Liverpool working to complete deal for Bradley Barcola - with France star open to move but PSG demanding £140MILLION

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool are working to reach an agreement with Paris Saint-Germain over Bradley Barcola amid escalating valuations.

The 23-year-old France international has indicated he does not wish to sign a new contract with the European champions and is open to joining Liverpool, who have a long-held interest.

PSG are considering his sale but he still has two years left on his contract and they believe, based on his age, potential and current market prices, £140million is a fair reflection of his valuation.

Liverpool will seek a compromise on that with Barcola's price reputed to have been closer to £75million last summer when they first sounded out his representatives.

Barcola is not a regular starter for Luis Enrique's side and they have been pursuing RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande, which would have pushed him further down the pecking order, only for Real Madrid to declare their intent to sign the Ivory Coast international on Friday – which is now close to completion.

Liverpool also had an £85million proposal rejected for Diomande, but Barcola has always been in their thinking.

Liverpool are working to complete a deal for £140million-rated PSG winger Bradley Barcola

He has the skillset to suit Andoni Iraola's style and can provide a serious goal threat following the void left by Mo Salah's departure.

Arsenal and Bayern Munich also retain interest in Barcola while Chelsea made enquiries earlier in the summer.

The Gunners are currently exploring the possibility of signing Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid. Such a deal would require significant investment.

They also retain ambitious interest in Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez. However, it is understood Barcola would like to speak to Liverpool if they can agree terms with PSG.

Sports.title: Besiktas need answer from Mohamed Salah after making their final offer, Saudi club Al-Rayyan target Jadon Sancho... and Inter confirm they want Cristian Romero from Tottenham: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Liverpool want compromise on Barcola

Liverpool are working to find agreement with Paris Saint-Germain over Bradley Barcola amid escalating valuations.

The 23-year-old France international has indicated he does not wish to sign a new contract with the European champions and is open to joining Liverpool who have a long-held interest.

PSG are considering his sale but he still has two years left on contract and they believe, based on his age, potential and current market prices, £140million is a fair reflection of his valuation.

Liverpool will seek a compromise on that with Barcola's price reputed to have been closer to £75m last summer when they first sounded out his representatives.

Read more on this story HERE

Bradley Barcola has indicated he will not sign a new contract at Paris Saint-Germain

Inter in for Tottenham star Romero

Inter Milan have confirmed they have entered talks with Tottenham over the potential signing of Cristian Romero.

The Spurs captain helped Argentina reach a second straight World Cup final this month, but as Daily Mail Sport reported last month is attracting interest from the Italian giants after they were made aware he could leave this summer.

The structure is complicated, though, as Spurs still want a significant fee for the 28-year-old after an eventful five-year spell.

Inter’s sporting director, Piero Ausilio, told Sky Italy: 'It’s definitely a deal we are trying to sign with the player and the club. These things take some time but there’s definitely interest. Let’s see.'

Is it yes or no, Mo? Besiktas waiting for Salah answer

Besiktas say they are awaiting Mohamed Salah's decision after submitting their final offer for the former Liverpool forward.

Club president Serdal Adali confirmed to Turkish media: 'We told Salah and his agent that we expect them to inform us of their decision shortly.

'Since our first meetings, we have evaluated every requested increase and amendment within the framework of Besiktas' interests and presented our final offer. The decision is now on the player's side, and we expect a response soon.'

He added that Besiktas had reviewed every requested increase and amendment throughout the negotiations while keeping the club's interests in mind before putting forward its last proposal.

It is understood Besiktas are the first choice for Salah, now 34, but he does have offers from elsewhere - including the MLS, where Sporting Kansas City have made a lucrative two-year contract proposal.

Mo Salah left Liverpool at the end of last season and has offers from more than one club

Saudi suitor for Sancho

Jason Sancho has emerged as a target for Qatari club Al-Rayyan.

The 26-year-old is a free agent after leaving Manchester United and has been keeping fit while awaiting offers to assess.

Atletico Madrid have also shown an interest in the England international.

Jadon Sancho had loan spells at Dortmund, Chelsea and Aston Villa in his final three seasons as a Manchester United player

Blackburn bag Finley after trial

Blackburn Rovers have signed former Brighton goalkeeper Finley Taylor after he impressed on trial.

The 18-year-old was a free agent having left Brighton, where he had been for five years.

Taylor said: 'At the end of last season, I came on trial, played against Manchester United and it was a good game. A tough game against obviously one of the best teams in England.

'After that, I found out I got signed. It was just a phone call, and it was a massive relief because, obviously, when you leave a club before, it's quite nerve-racking; you don't know what to expect. So, to get that call was a massive relief.'

Newcastle look at Hornicek after he rejected Hull move

Newcastle United have switched sights to Sporting Braga goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek.

The 24-year-old Czech Republic international was the subject of a failed bid by Hull City earlier in the window and Benfica have been making enquiries in the past week.

Hull even matched his £25.9m release clause but Hornicek turned down the move.

'We even had one [a concrete approach]. The player himself, Hornicek, refused. There was a proposal from England, from the Premier League, but the player felt he shouldn’t go to that club and we were happy for him to stay,' the Braga president António Salvador confirmed to Portuguese media.

Lukas Hornicek went to the World Cup with Czech Republic and has a £29.5m release clause at Braga

Hornicek was back in action in midweek as he starred in Braga's 1-0 win at Serbian side Zeleznicar Pancevo in their Europa Conference League qualifier.

Newcastle had been pursuing Manchester City's James Trafford but he is set on moving to Leeds United in a deal worth around £45m as he discusses inserting a release clause into his contract.

They had also held a meeting over Brighton keeper Carl Rushworth but ultimately Newcastle had reservations about his lack of top flight experience. Rushworth remains a target for Coventry City, where he was on loan last season. They have had bids worth £25m rejected so far.

Newcastle have now asked about Hornicek and the deal could be agreed quickly if all parties wish to proceed.

Wrexham in for Palace's Imray - but face competition

Wrexham have joined the clubs showing interest in Crystal Palace full-back Danny Imray.

The 22-year-old, who had loan spells with Blackpool and West Bromwich Albion last season, is wanted back by Albion while Stoke City have also posted interest.

Wrexham, though, are continuing to push the bar on their targets as they try to take that next step up into the Premier League.

They also remain in the chase for Leicester City's Harry Souttar. The Australia international has asked to leave but the Foxes want £10million which is deterring suitors such as Sheffield United, Stoke City and more.

Danny Imray

Leicester in race against time for No 9

Leicester City are clear favourites to gain promotion from League One but are still to sign a striker - with barely three weeks to go until they kick-off the season against Notts County.

Manager Russell Martin may have overseen a 3-3 draw against La Liga side Malaga in Marbella on Saturday but that didn't mask what he thought the former Premier League champions were missing.

'The topline, both wide positions and a No 9, I think it’s really clear,' said the Foxes' boss when asked about priorities.

They have tried and failed to agree terms with former West Ham striker Danny Ings and, despite his appearance at first-team testing, Jamie Vardy is not planning a return. He still has aspirations to finish at the top.

Sports.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty says getting back into Olympic medal contention is 'the hardest climb I've ever faced'... after breaking down in tears at Commonwealth Games bronze
Sports.content:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty claimed he faces the toughest challenge of his career to get back into medal contention for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

The 31-year-old broke down in tears after finishing third in the men’s 100m breaststroke final, having held the world record since 2015.

Britain’s iconic swimmer will have another shot at gold over 50m on Monday night, having qualified second on his semi-final on Sunday evening, and he is desperate to prove that time has not caught up with him.

‘It's been hard,’ said Ramsay-Peaty after the 100m final. ‘There have been a multitude of things at play over the last few years — burnout, breaking my foot, fighting against something that you love.

'Coming back to where I am now and making the decision to go for LA, I think this is going to be the hardest climb I've ever faced and the hardest test. It's really hard to see the summit because it's so hard. I don't think anyone understands.’

Ramsay-Peaty’s wife, Holly – the daughter of celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay – has been in Glasgow to watch the races. Fatherhood has shifted the breast-stroker's priorities but he does not plan to retire before the next Olympics.

Adam Ramsay-Peaty has said getting back into Olympic medal contention is 'the hardest climb I've ever faced'

‘There are just a lot of personal and professional things that I need to pull together and work out what's important, and what the long-term goal is for my happiness and for my immediate family's happiness as well,' he added.

‘When your world record is three seconds away, we've got to seriously ask what's going wrong because that's not me. We need to look at it, interrogate it, look at the data, and ask whether it was an issue with race pace, fitness, or something else.

'I don't think it was fitness, but there are a lot of components that make us swim, so we really have to analyse it. Of course I'm committed. I've got a big fight in me, and normally it only takes me 24 hours to turn things around.’

He struck a more positive note after breezing into the 50m breaststroke final on Sunday evening, finishing second in his semi-final behind South Africa's Michael Houlie in a time of 26.82sec.

'I think the last 24 hours have been a bit of a whirlwind,' said Ramsay-Peaty. 'It's not something I'm used to, to be honest. I guess this sport is not really about when you get beaten because it's going to be inevitable. Essentially (what's important is) how long it takes you to look at it and turn it around for tonight. And we're really happy with that, we're on a great trajectory for tomorrow.

'Every time I race I am getting a little bit stronger - apart from yesterday - which is important, but I am getting more exposed to it. And people forget that I haven't done this for two years, you know. Even I forget that. So I think that perspective is a good thing to handle tomorrow. Tell you what, I'll just enjoy the crowd. It's an amazing crowd.'

Sports.title: Lucky Lando Norris WINS the Hungarian Grand Prix after team-mate Oscar Piastri's spectacular capitulation - while Kimi Antonelli gains the upper hand on title rivals Lewis Hamilton and George Russell
Sports.content:
Lucky Lando Norris WINS the Hungarian Grand Prix after team-mate Oscar Piastri's spectacular capitulation - while Kimi Antonelli gains the upper hand on title rivals Lewis Hamilton and George Russell

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Lucky, lucky, Lando. Not that world champion Norris was other than often the fastest hound in the Hungarian Grand Prix and should have won it on his own.

But he was helped, first, by a bizarre incident befalling his McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri handing him the victory chance his pole position deserved and his poor opening lap, sorry, did not.

This first of two pivotal moments in Norris’s triumph came on lap 38 when Piastri, who had pitted for a second time, was trying to make progress back into the lead. Williams’ Carlos Sainz – the villain of the piece – was fighting with Fernando Alonso for 15th and in his path.

Distracted by his skirmish, Sainz was oblivious of Piastri poised to lap him. It was blue-flag time. The Spaniard should have yielded. He did not.

Piastri fumed: ‘Get out of the f***ing way, you idiot.’ They banged tyres. ‘Oh, my God!’

Lando Norris returned to the top step of the podium with a dominant win in Hungary

The British driver was stunned by team-mate Oscar Piastri but wrestled back control

All this confusion was delaying Piastri, obviously, while Norris was making hay out where the sun shone. After Norris was called in at the end of the following lap, he emerged in front of the other papaya car. Job done.

Piastri was furious. Obviously with Sainz. But also, it seemed, with his McLaren team for granting Norris freedom to open up an advantage for seven laps after his own stop.

Piastri’s race engineer Tom Stallard came on the radio, to pacify him, saying: ‘Oscar, it’s Sainz that cost us. Target is to get to the end on these tyres.’

Piastri rejoined: ‘Oh, mate, just don’t talk to me now.

‘Nice of you guys to factor that one (the traffic) in by the way, thanks.’

If he believes the team pull for Norris, their hand-reared champion, rather than him, this reverse would hardly have put his mind to rest.

The second and final slice of luck working for Norris came as Piastri, who seemed set to finish second, conked out with a gearbox problem, his race over on lap 56 of 70.

Thus, without any concerns at all, Norris went on to claim the first win of his title defence, indeed since the Sao Paulo Grand Prix last November.

Now more drama ensued as a virtual safety car was enlisted. Lewis Hamilton, on a unravelling weekend for him given what riches it promised, had succeeded the stricken Piastri in the running order.

This was not to last. Norris came in for new tyres and so did Hamilton. For Norris, fine, back out in top spot. But Hamilton emerged from the pits virtually level with third-placed Kimi Antonelli, and, although the seven-time world champion pushed himself ahead of the Italian into and out of the first corner, it was not legit.

Was he speeding in the pits? He was placed under investigation for the suspected offence and handed a five-second penalty a few minutes later. ‘They are handing out penalties like crazy,’ said Hamilton, though he later relented in his criticism of the beak.

He had already been told by his pit wall to hand the place back to Antonelli, but that is not quite how it stayed: yes, Norris took the flag first, Max Verstappen second (because he did not stop under the VSC) and Antonelli third. But Hamilton’s penalty dropped him below team-mate Charles Leclerc and into fifth place.

What a headache for Hamilton, who had started where he was condemned to finish after being demoted three places on Saturday for inadvertently blocking Piastri in qualifying. Instead of clipping Antonelli’s championship lead by six points, as he was due to do prior to the Australian’s retirement, he fell five points back. He is 50 behind Antonelli heading into the sport’s summer holidays.

A thought: why didn’t Ferrari slow down Leclerc? Do they not want to win the drivers’ title?

George Russell, seventh on the day, is now 59 adrift, nine points down on his starting position. Not great for the Briton, but not the worst outcome given how he watched the field fly by him at the start as anti-stall kicked in on his Mercedes. He went down to 19th at the end of lap one, but, helped by a new engine fitted after qualifying, came through the midfield.

‘I am past the point of disappointment now,’ said Russell, with a resigned smile. ‘If I continue to be disappointed with everything that goes on, I’ll be disappointed every day of the week.

‘My pace was as strong as anyone out there, and I haven’t been there for the past two or three races, so I will take the positives there. But it is unbelievable the list of things that have gone wrong this season.

Norris benefited from Oscar Piastri's spectacular capitulation on Sunday afternoon

Lewis Hamilton fell further back in the championship race to Kimi Antonelli

‘I was on the throttle holding the revs, and four seconds before the lights went out the engines started revving all over the place – the engine wasn’t reacting to the throttle. It is a brand new engine. No idea.’

There was little overtaking to savour, though Verstappen made a brilliant pass on Hamilton at the first corner – named after his (Verstappen’s) de facto father-in-law Nelson Piquet. He caught the Briton by surprise, a typical Max mugging.

Piastri did not need to exert such virtuosity as an old Norris habit came back to haunt him, namely his weakness on first laps that has repeatedly cost him wins from promising starting positions, especially in 2024 when he had an outside chance of claiming the title a year before he did.

Norris was very smartly away from pole and took the first corner in command. But he drifted wide at the second bend, named after Hamilton, and Piastri assumed the lead.

Norris possessed more pace than his team-mate and harried him, but Piastri held track position until his afternoon unknotted itself. Norris finally streaked away, finishing 15 seconds up the road and out of sight, a smile back on the champion’s face after a welcome victory of persistence and pace as well as good fortune.

Sports.title: Chelsea ready to demand major fee for Pedro Neto amid Liverpool and Man City interest - as former boss Enzo Maresca eyes reunion
Sports.content:
Chelsea are not surprised by the reported interest in Pedro Neto, though would not allow their winger to leave on the cheap after noting the rising valuations of other wide men in this window.

The Premier League club are not actively touting their Portuguese 26-year-old for sale, but Blues insiders are aware of the asking prices being issued elsewhere in Europe, and specifically for RB Leipzig’s Yan Diomande and Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola.

Diomande and Barcola are both considered £100million-plus players by their respective clubs, and while Neto would struggle to fetch such a large fee, it does give Chelsea an idea of their own wide man’s worth. The Blues have not quoted a valuation on Neto as of yet.

Chelsea sources believe it is only natural that Neto has attracted interest because of a lack of top wingers in the current market.

City are also now managed by Enzo Maresca, who favoured Neto as his right winger while in charge at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea are not surprised at interest in Pedro Neto but will not allow him to leave on the cheap

New Man City boss Enzo Maresca favoured Neto on the right wing while in charge of Chelsea

Sports.title: Frustrated Lewis Hamilton demands answers from Ferrari after strategy call costs him dear in Hungary in chase for record eighth world title
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton pledged to seek answers from his Ferrari team after another missed opportunity in his spluttering quest for a record eighth world title.

The British driver fell 50 points behind championship leader Kimi Antonelli in Hungary by finishing fifth following a curious late strategy call that cost him a possible second place behind race winner Lando Norris.

While Norris was bathed in smiles after notching his first victory of his title defence, Hamilton was cursing his luck on a weekend that promised so much more than it delivered.

'Yes, it was a missed opportunity,' admitted Hamilton.

His weekend was compromised when he failed to land pole that looked to be at his mercy on a favourite track suited to his car and was then demoted down the field for impeding McLaren's Oscar Piastri in qualifying.

Starting fifth, he had come through to second place when Piastri's car broke down. He was called in by Ferrari for a new set of tyres and lost track position to Max Verstappen and Antonelli, who held on for second and third places.

Lewis Hamilton is seeking answers from Ferrari after a strategy call cost him in Hungary

Hamilton was then handed a five-second penalty for speeding in the pit lane – 0.01kph over the mandated 80kph (50mph) – as he charged back on the track after his late stop. That dropped him a further place behind team-mate Charles Leclerc.

'I definitely don't think we should have taken a stop,' said Hamilton, as the strategy blunder cost him a likely 11 points in relation to Antonelli.

'I got the call right at the pit-lane entry and I did not have time to debate it.

'I would never have stopped if it meant I would give up track position.

'We probably would have lost out to Max because he was on fresher tyres. But I may have been able to hold on to second, but it most likely would have been third. We have lost a whole bunch of points. We should have stayed out. I need to see why the team pulled me in.

'I had the pace to compete at least for the top two, top three.'

Hamilton's penalty yesterday was his fourth on successive weekends dating back to his false start at Silverstone. He was then harshly adjudged to have caused an accident with George Russell at Spa prior to his double punishments here at the Hungaroring.

Was he aggrieved by the stewards?

Hamilton was called in to change his tyres but failed to regain the places he lost in doing so

'No,' he said. 'The last three races have been pretty bad from my side. Silverstone was my fault at the start.

'At the last race, even the driver I collided with said it was a racing incident and they gave me a penalty. That was not needed. And that's cost me a lot of points.

'Saturday (blocking Piastri) was unfortunate. I take responsibility. I should have looked in my mirrors. But I got the information when he was behind me. It was a communication error.

'I will work hard to come back, to reset. There are still lots of positives to take.'

Sports.title: Michael Carrick meets Ole Gunnar Solskjaer after beating Man Utd legend to manager's job
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick meets Ole Gunnar Solskjaer after beating Man Utd legend to manager's job

Michael Carrick is currently in the midst of preparations for his first full season as Manchester United boss and has been reunited with another former Red Devils manager

View 2 Images Michael Carrick served as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's assistant at Old Trafford (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick was reunited with Ole Gunnar Solksjaer in Norway this week, just months after beating him to the manager’s job at Old Trafford. The Premier League side have been in Norway over the past few days as part of their pre-season preparations.

‌



The Red Devils took on Rosenborg on Friday and secured a 5-0 success, with Shea Lacey, Joshua Zirkzee, Jacob Devaney, Harry Amass and Ethan Williams all finding the net.

‌



Away from taking on the Norwegians, United boss Carrick also had more on his mind. As per the Manchester Evening News, he met up with former head coach Solskjaer.

‌



The pair are thought to have a close relationship, despite Carrick having beaten the former forward to the top job at Old Trafford last season. It was suggested that Solskjaer was in talks regarding a second stint in charge.

But Red Devils chiefs opted for Carrick instead and he was handed the job on a permanent basis after 12 wins from 17 games - form that was good enough to see United seal a spot back in the Champions League.

Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star READ MORE :

Carrick’s reunion with Solskjaer comes after he admitted that he had sought after advice from the Norwegian ahead of officially taking the reins at Old Trafford.

‌



Speaking earlier this year, he said: “Yeah, yeah I’ve spoken to him. We’re close, we’ve been through a lot together. He’s been fully supportive, as you’d expect. He’s some man, I respect him an awful lot. He wished us all the best, and he was happy that we got the right result.

“I think, friendships, you have conversations… I’ve got a lot of friends in places that I can pick on if I need to. I’m not that one that bothers a lot of people to be honest, but… He’s certainly there if ever I need.”

Speaking after United’s emphatic victory against Rosenborg, Carrick said: “Clean sheet, scoring goals, and everyone, by the looks of it, coming through injury-free is what you want at this stage, really.

‌



View 2 Images Michael Carrick has met with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer during United's time in Norway (Image: Getty Images)

“As much as we want everything to improve and performances to be better all the time, I think keeping players fit and progressing through pre-season is as important as anything.

“So, two games in, two weeks in, I think we can take where we are and we’re pretty happy. The second half, the younger players coming on, I thought they were fantastic. They played as a team really well and deserve what they got second half.”

‌



He added: “It’s important to build through this pre-season, some players need more minutes than others as they go and we’re managing some players a little bit more than others. I've said it before the game, it's never going to be perfect, two weeks in and you're kind of building towards that.

“So, I thought there was a lot of good things, some of the goals were fantastic goals and it’s just as pleasing to keep a clean sheet. So yeah, we’re moving forward nicely.”

Sports.title: Tyson Fury's X-rated two-word response to Anthony Joshua with fight on
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury's X-rated two-word response to Anthony Joshua with fight on

After Anthony Joshua came close to losing his must win fight against Kristian Prenga, Tyson Fury only had two words for the bout

View 2 Images Tyson Fury has made his thoughts onrival Anthony Joshua's recent performance clear (Image: YouTube/Boxing King Media)

Tyson Fury only had two words after seeing Kristian Prenga deal Anthony Joshua one of the biggest scares of his career - "Wow, wtf?"

‌



Fury commented those words on social media after Ring Magazine chief and Zuffa boxing co-founder Turki Alalshikh uploaded a highlights package of Joshua's win over Prenga. The Albanian scored two huge knockdowns over AJ in the first round, the biggest of which coming in the opening exchanges.

‌



Prenga stepped inside Joshua and caught him with a perfect uppercut which sent the two-time unified heavyweight champion tumbling to the canvas, before catching him with another huge shot later in the round. However, Joshua got his bearings and knocked the 35-year-old out in round two with a vicious combination.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Oleksandr Usyk, whose team has been training Joshua since December, breathed a huge sigh of relief after Joshua's victory was confirmed. Meanwhile, Fury only let his thoughts be known on Instagram by commenting "Wow, wtf?" on the video on Alalshikh's post.

At present, that's the Gypsy King's only comment on Joshua's brush with disaster against Prenga. The Olympic gold medallist needed to be victorious to ensure the blockbuster clash with Fury would take place.

‌



The night before, Fury held up his end of the bargain by easily stopping Mariusz Wach in their non-televised clash in Pattaya, Thailand. The 46-year-old Pole gave up on his stool at the end of the seventh round after his team decided he had taken enough punishment from Fury.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

The boxing world held its breath in anticipation for Fury to turn up ringside in Jeddah to confront Joshua. The latter also instantly looked for Fury in the arena straight after beating him, only for him not to be there.

‌



Channelling his inner Mike Tyson, Joshua took the microphone and said: "Wait a minute - have we got Tyson Fury in the room? Wait, wait, wait, to more important matters - is he here or not? Fair do’s.

"Im'ma rip his heart out. I'm the meanest and vicious champion's ever been. Listen, all jokes aside, you see, there’s two sides of this thing. One is fire. You have to have that vim, that grrr. But also respect.

View 2 Images Joshua was knocked down twice in the first round (Image: Matchroom Boxing/Getty Images)

‌



"I respect everything he has done. And everything that he has achieved. As someone who who has been calling for the fight for a long time, we're here now. Shout out to his Excellency. Shout to Eddie Hearn for making these opportunities possible, and I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat.”

Joshua's promoter Hearn has insisted all of the contracts have been signed, but a date or location is yet to be confirmed. UK boxing fans have been hoping for the clash to be in London, but Madison Square Garden in New York has also emerged as a potential venue.

Sports.title: Liverpool identify Bradley Barcola transfer alternative as ‘contact made’ with agent
Sports.content:
Liverpool identify Bradley Barcola transfer alternative as ‘contact made’ with agent

Liverpool are among the clubs linked with Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola as they attempt to find a replacement for Mo Salah but a deal could be very costly, forcing the Reds to look elsewhere

View 2 Images Liverpool have been told to pay £140m for Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool are looking at Juventus star Francisco Conceicao as an alternative to Bradley Barcola, who could cost as much as £140million. The Reds are keen to add to their wide options this summer following Mohamed Salah’s exit a year before the end of his contract.

‌



Liverpool completed a deal for Spanish wideman Victor Munoz for £34.5m last month, albeit they still want to sign another forward. Bayern Munich’s Michael Olise has been linked, albeit the German giants are not keen on selling.

‌



Leipzig’s Yan Diomande was also an option but he now appears set for a move to Real Madrid. Paris Saint-Germain’s Barcola has also emerged as a priority target, but the French club’s £140m price tag is putting the Merseysiders off.

‌



That has forced Liverpool to look elsewhere. According to reports in Italy, Juventus’ Conceicao is seen as a cheaper option and they have already got in touch with his representatives regarding a deal.

Liverpool sent strong Michael Olise transfer warning by Bayern Munich chief READ MORE :

As it stands, Juventus are not keen on selling, having only spent £27.3m to sign him permanently last summer following an initial loan move from Porto. But it is thought that an offer in the region of around €50m (£42.6m) could be enough to seal his services.

It is not the first time that Liverpool have been linked with a swoop for Conceicao. His name was also mentioned during last season but the Portuguese international remained tight-lipped on his future.

‌



He said: “I know people talk about a big club, but I play for a big club where I am happy. At the moment I am only focused on these two games with the national team and then I will focus on the final stretch of the season to help my club as much as possible.”

View 2 Images Francisco Conceicao has been linked with Juventus on a number of occasions (Image: Getty Images)

“I am at a big club where the pressure to win is very high. I just have to keep working and contribute with goals and assists.

‌



“My objective is to help with goals and assists, that is what I try to do. I must continue every day to show that I have the ability to help the national team and be helped by them to keep improving.”

Conceicao, 23, has made 82 appearances for Juventus in all and has scored 11 goals in all competitions. His contract with the Italian giants is set to run until the summer of 2030.

Sports.title: Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star
Sports.content:
With the Premier League on course to smash its spending record, it's worth reminding them that you don't always have to splash out on signings. Sometimes the best transfers cost nothing - well, bar a hefty a signing-on bonus.

From Ruud Gullit to Chelsea and Sol Campbell to Arsenal, to James Milner to Liverpool and Zlatan Ibrahimovic to Manchester United, the Premier League has seen its fair share of excellent free transfers down the years.

So who could be next? There are plenty of stars from around the world who find themselves without a club, some of them more familiar to English sides than others.

As the final month of the summer transfer window nears, let's build an XI of free agents.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool sent strong Michael Olise transfer warning by Bayern Munich chief READ MORE :

Goalkeeper: Stefan Ortega

Perhaps the least stacked position in this team, former Manchester City and Nottingham Forest star Stefan Ortega looks the standout goalkeeper available on a free. Ex-Brighton shot-stopper Matthew Ryan is another looking for his next move, while former Aston Villa man Orjan Nyland will hope that his World Cup performances convince someone to come knocking.

Right-back: Dani Carvajal

Arguably the best right-back of his generation, Dani Carvajal left Real Madrid this summer after two spells covering 23 years in which he won 27 major trophies. The Spaniard has reportedly received proposals from the Saudi Pro League, Major League Soccer and Inter Milan, but he remains out of work.

Centre-back: John Stones

John Stones was a somewhat surprise inclusion in the England squad after making just 38 appearances in his final two seasons with Manchester City, but he ended up starting both the quarter-finals and semi-finals in a show of faith from Thomas Tuchel. His experience and quality on the ball makes him an attractive prospect for clubs willing to take a risk on his dubious fitness, with Chelsea and Arsenal linked.

‌



Which club should sign John Stones? Have your say in the comments section.

View 5 Images John Stones was released by Manchester City (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

Centre-back: David Alaba

Another departure from Madrid, David Alaba's last three years have been ravaged by injury, missing a total of 126 games for club and country. The ex-Bayern Munich star still managed to be a starter at the World Cup, so that may well convince another European giant to snap him up.

Left-back: Oleksandr Zinchenko

Two clubs, 12 games and one serious injury - that was the story of Oleksandr Zinchenko's season. Following a disappointing loan spell with Nottingham Forest, Arsenal sold him to Ajax for just £1.3million.

‌



But the Ukrainian was only given a short-term deal before suffering a knee injury which is set to rule him out for well into the new season. Zinchenko has proven himself in the Premier League, but will his rehab put clubs off signing him this summer?

View 5 Images Injury ruined Oleksandr Zinchenko's spell with Ajax before it got going (Image: Roy Lazet/Soccrates/Getty Images)

Centre midfield: Franck Kessie

Franck Kessie knows all about getting a big move on a free transfer. The Ivorian moved to Barcelona after his contract with AC Milan expired in 2022, and he memorably scored the goal that won Xavi Hernandez's side the La Liga title in his one and only season.

Kessie was then sold to Saudi Arabian side Al-Ahli, where he spent the past three seasons. But now he's without a club and tipped for a return to Italy with Juventus.

‌



Centre midfield: Leon Goretzka

After eight years and 15 trophies with Bayern Munich, Leon Goretzka is another free agent with serious pedigree to offer. The German went to the World Cup but has been tipped for an immediate return to the United States, with Chicago Fire heavily linked with what would be their second marquee signing of the summer after acquiring Robert Lewandowski.

View 5 Images Leon Goretzka went to the World Cup with Germany (Image: Joe Prior/Visionhaus via Getty Images)

Centre midfield: Julian Brandt

Staying in the Bundesliga and Julian Brandt has left Borussia Dortmund. The versatile playmaker is said to have offers from Leeds and Ajax, while Arsenal, Aston Villa and Barcelona have also been linked.

Midfield is where some real bargains are to be had. Other options include Yves Bissouma, Dani Ceballos, Fabinho and Lorenzo Pellegrini.

‌



Right wing: Mo Salah

No doubt the most high-profile name in this team, Mo Salah still hasn't found a new club three months after his departure from Liverpool was announced. For a player of his stature and still impeccably fit at 34 years old, that's a surprise.

But factor in the World Cup and it's understandable that the Egypt captain has had other priorities. Speculation over his next destination has been building in the past fortnight, though, with Sporting Kansas City lining up an ambition move and cash-rich Saudi clubs also keen.

According to reports, his priority to stay in Europe. Could a Premier League club offer him a deal?

View 5 Images Mo Salah has left Liverpool after nine years (Image: Jack Thomas/Getty Images)

‌



Striker: Dusan Vlahovic

When Juventus paid £66m for Dusan Vlahovic in 2022, few doubted that he'd become one of Europe's most prolific No.9s. But fast forward four years and he's without an employer.

Barcelona continue to be linked with the ex-Fiorentina marksman while there's been speculation that Juventus could resume talks over a new contract, having failed to agree on an extension before the end of the season. Watch this space.

Left wing: Jadon Sancho

Finally, a name more than familiar to English fans. Jadon Sancho's deal with Manchester United ran out last month and Aston Villa, who he spent last season on loan with, don't want to sign him permanently.

A return to former club Borussia Dortmund has long been rumoured, having also had a loan spell there in 2024. Sancho is still just 26 and has plenty of magic to offer if he can find the right landing spot this summer.

‌

Sports.title: Liverpool and Arsenal alerted after Bradley Barcola transfer call as PSG seek record fee
Sports.content:
Liverpool and Arsenal alerted after Bradley Barcola transfer call as PSG seek record fee

Liverpool and Arsenal have both been linked with Bradley Barcola, who will be allowed to leave PSG this summer provided his £140m price tag is met

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola's price tag has been set by PSG (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

PSG have slapped a mammoth £140million price tag on Bradley Barcola as it looks increasingly like he will leave the Champions League winners.

‌



The winger has been the subject of interest from the likes of Liverpool and Arsenal this summer but his place at the Parisians is in jeopardy and an exit in expected over the coming months. He's confirmed he won't signed a new deal and PSG want to maximise their profits if he does depart.

‌



Real Madrid and PSG are battling to land RB Leipzig’s Yan Diomande, who is also on Liverpool's radar, but a move to Paris would further push Barcola down the pecking order.

‌



His refusal to sign a new deal, even though he's under contract until 2031, has seen PSG willing to see him leave provided their huge price tag is met, reports the Evening Standard.

PSG believe their huge valuation, which would make Barcola their most expensive sale ever, is fair given what they've seen elsewhere in the market. The winger has ultimately helped deliver successive European Cups and is still only 23. The Parisians have watched Morgan Rogers and Elliot Anderson move for £117m and £116m respectively.

Barcola caught the eye with an impressive World Cup campaign as France made it to the semi-finals, scoring three times. Liverpool are thought to be in pole position to sign Barcola with Diomande preferring other destinations and Arsenal looking to prioritise a move for Vinicius Jnr.

‌



Last term he scored 13 times, which came after a year where he found the net 21 times, even though he was not a guaranteed starter under Luis Enrique.

View 2 Images PSG want to land Yan Diomande, which would push Bradley Barcola further down the pecking order (Image: Getty Images)

Last year the PSG boss had to warn off rivals from signing Barcola, insisting he was crucial to his plans. He was utilised throughout last season, but ultimately sits behind the likes of Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in the pecking order.

Article continues below

Liverpool are on the lookout for a man to replace Mohamed Salah, who left after almost a decade at Anfield. They've shown in recent years that they are prepared to spend big on players, but landing Barcola could see them break their own British transfer record.
