World.title: Berlin police shoot dead chief suspect in deadly Islamist Pride attack
World.content:
Berlin – German police said Sunday they had shot and killed the chief suspect in what officials described as a deadly Islamist attack near the Berlin Pride parade the previous night, the latest ramming assault to hit the country.

The attack late Saturday — the first such incident to target the German capital’s LGBTQ community — killed one woman and wounded 29 others.

Berlin police said on X that they had traced the chief suspect, 21-year old Abdul Ballout, to an allotment complex in the western Spandau district at around 6:00 pm (1600 GMT) on Sunday.

Ballout “ran towards them with a bladed weapon”, the police said, prompting officers to open fire, “injuring the suspect so that he died at the scene despite attempts to rescusitate him”.

Earlier, prosecutors had said that Ballout, a German citizen of Lebanese origin, had been a supporter of the so-called Islamic State group (IS) with several criminal convictions, the latest dating from May.

Saturday’s attack shattered what had been a day of celebration for hundreds of thousands attending Christopher Street Day (CSD), one of Europe’s largest Pride events.

Politicians in Germany and elsewhere in Europe widely condemned the attack, while the flag at the German Bundestag was lowered to half mast.

Speaking before a memorial service for the victims at Berlin’s Marienkirche church, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz appealed to those targeted by the attack to “not let yourselves be intimidated”.

– Suspect’s criminal past –

Shortly before 10:00 pm (2000 GMT) on Saturday a white minivan ran into people on the southern edge of central Berlin’s Tiergarten park before crashing into a tree.

Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said Ballout was suspected of having then used a machete to attack more people.

Dobrindt said 29 people were injured, some seriously.

Merz said Sunday evening that none of the victims were any longer in a life-threatening condition.

The attack took place several hundred metres away from the end of the tightly guarded CSD parade route and the event’s main stage at Berlin’s Brandenburg Gate.

Dobrindt said Ballout had been known to the authorities for a “high number” of previous crimes and for being radicalised.

“Everything we see here indicates that this was an Islamist terror attack,” he said.

Prosecutors said Ballout had previous convictions for bodily harm and extortion committed in 2019, and one for robbery in 2020.

They say that in 2024 he shared IS propaganda on Instagram and the following year travelled to Lebanon in order to fight for the militia in Syria.

He was arrested in Lebanon and sentenced to three months’ prison.

On his return to Germany in November he was arrested and held until his conviction in May for “preparing a serious act of subversive violence”.

But his sentence of one year and ten months in jail was suspended, partially in recognition of the time he had spent in jail in Lebanon and pre-trial detention, and partially because he had admitted to the crimes and distanced himself from IS.

– ‘Won’t beat us down’ –

In a vigil on Sunday afternoon, hundreds of people packed the square in front of the Brandenburg Gate holding rainbow flags and flowers with more gathering nearby.

Luka, a 23-year-old student, told AFP she hoped the attack wouldn’t be exploited by the surging anti-immigration far-right ahead of elections in the capital and in several regions in September.

At the scene of the attack itself people left flowers and hand-written messages of condolence and support.

Armin Duenhoelter, 49 from Wolfsburg, who works as a drag artist, was backstage at the main stage when the attack cut short the celebrations.

He told AFP early Sunday that he was still shocked but vowed to be back for next year’s CSD.

“We won’t let it beat us down,” he said.

– Spate of attacks –

Saturday’s attack revived memories of a string of similar incidents which have shaken Germany in recent years and inflamed debate on immigration, with several of the perpetrators being from outside Germany.

Martin Hess, a lawmaker from the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), denounced the attack as a result of “a complete failure of the government’s security policies”.

The deadliest attack in recent years was a truck rampage at a Berlin Christmas market in December 2016 by a Tunisian man with jihadist motives that killed 13 people.

The run-up to last year’s general election saw a spate of attacks in public places, including by attackers with Islamist motives.

In 2024, a Saudi psychiatrist and anti-Islam activist killed six people and wounded more than 300 in a car-ramming at a busy Christmas market in the eastern city of Magdeburg.

World.title: Iraq, Lebanon discuss economic partnerships
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said on Sunday that it is important to establish economic partnerships with Lebanon in different sectors.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during discussions held in Baghdad with Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam and his accompanying delegation, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The two leaders co-chaired discussions between the two countries, where ministers from both sides attended.

The discussions focused on improving bilateral ties in economic, political, and security areas. They also addressed approaches to strengthen the two countries’ partnership to promote comprehensive and long-term development and benefit both the Iraqi and Lebanese people.

Al-Zaidi also highlighted Iraq and Lebanon’s close friendship, dedication to development, and the need to form beneficial economic collaborations across all development areas.

The prime minister also emphasized the importance of joint coordination between the two nations in addressing regional challenges and supporting efforts to boost stability, reduce tensions, and resolve disputes.

World.title: Washington rejects Iraq’s deal with Turkmenistan to import gas
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s plan to purchase Turkmen gas has encountered another obstacle, as the US has raised objections to Baghdad’s proposal to transport the supplies through Iranian territory.

A source told Attaqa News that the United States has connected the agreement’s execution to negotiating a comprehensive political solution with Tehran, complicating the issue of obtaining the fuel required to run Iraq’s power plants.

The US position emerged during talks held in Washington by a government delegation accompanying Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, which included Electricity Minister Ali Wahib and Oil Minister Basim Khudair.

The two sides discussed energy and economic cooperation, but the Turkmen gas sale to Iraq via Iran drew strong American opposition, despite Baghdad’s urgent need for new fuel sources amid a worsening electricity crisis.

The rejection comes amid escalating military operations in the Middle East, with the United States and Iran exchanging attacks, as well as rising tensions in the Arabian Gulf, which have affected maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iraq signed a memorandum of understanding in 2023 with Turkmenistan to import the necessary gas for its power plants, as stated by the Ministry of Electricity. The ministry indicated that the initiative will necessitate additional negotiations regarding the transportation of gas through Iran.

Power plants in Iraq depend on gas imports from Iran, which cover one-third of the country’s energy needs.

This agreement permits Iran to receive a quarter of the gas supplied across its borders.

The gas supply agreement with Turkmenistan aims to provide Iraq with an average of 20 million cubic meters per day.

World.title: Iraqi court seizes IQD 27 billion in Jumaili’s case
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s anti-corruption judiciary has seized IQD 27 billion in cash as part of an ongoing investigation involving Adnan Al-Jumaili, the detained former Deputy Oil Minister for Refining Affairs, in one of the country’s latest high-profile corruption cases.

Judicial authorities said the money was recovered during investigations into alleged financial losses linked to projects overseen by the former official and other individuals connected to the case.

In a statement issued on Sunday, the media office of Iraq’s judiciary said Judge Diaa Jaafar, the investigating judge at the Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Court, confirmed the seizure of IQD 27 billion.

According to the court, the funds were discovered after investigators traced financial proceeds allegedly generated through waste and irregularities in projects associated with Al-Jumaili and other suspects.

Officials said the cash had been hidden by several individuals believed to be involved in the case. The court said investigators are continuing to pursue additional suspects and trace other assets that may be linked to the alleged offenses.

Judicial authorities indicated that the investigation remains active as efforts continue to identify everyone involved and recover additional public funds, if any are found.

The judiciary also released photographs showing stacks of newly recovered banknotes arranged in large piles following the seizure. According to the statement, the images document the IQD 27 billion recovered during Sunday’s operation, which authorities said had been concealed by individuals connected to the former deputy minister.

Officials did not disclose how many people are under investigation or provide further details about the locations where the money was found.

The case is among several recent corruption investigations pursued by Iraq’s anti-corruption courts as authorities seek to recover public funds and hold officials accountable for alleged financial crimes.

The judiciary reiterated that investigations remain ongoing and that further legal action could follow as additional evidence emerges.

World.title: Iraq completes initial designs for Development Road Project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has completed the preliminary designs for its flagship Development Road Project and railway corridor, marking a major milestone as the government prepares to advance one of its largest infrastructure initiatives into the implementation phase.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Sunday that the initial designs are now 100% complete, with work shifting to detailed engineering plans covering infrastructure, bridges, railway stations, and technical facilities along the project’s route.

According to a source at the ministry’s media office, engineers have begun preparing the project’s detailed designs to ensure the corridor meets international engineering and construction standards. The next phase includes finalizing plans for the railway network, highways, bridges, stations, and supporting infrastructure before construction begins.

Officials described the transition as a key step toward launching the long-awaited project after completing the necessary preparatory stages.

The announcement follows a recent visit by Turkish Transport Minister Abdulkadir Uraloğlu to Baghdad on July 21, where he held talks with Iraqi officials on strengthening cooperation in transport and communications.

During the meetings, Iraqi Transport Minister Wahb Al-Hassani and his Turkish counterpart agreed to accelerate technical planning and implementation procedures for the Development Road Project.

The ministry said both sides consider the corridor a transformative initiative that could reshape regional trade and economic cooperation. The ministry also revealed that Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has instructed officials to prepare a comprehensive financing mechanism for the project.

Securing funding will be a priority ahead of the project’s implementation and is expected to feature prominently during Al-Zaidi’s upcoming visit to Ankara, where discussions with Turkish officials will focus on advancing strategic cooperation and moving the project toward construction.

The Development Road Project is designed to create a major transport corridor linking Iraq’s ports with regional and international markets. The combined railway and highway network aims to connect the Grand Faw Port in southern Iraq with Turkey and Europe, positioning Iraq as a key logistics hub between Asia and Europe.

Officials say the corridor will significantly improve trade flows while strengthening Iraq’s role in global supply chains. Alongside the engineering work, the Ministry of Transport is preparing the project’s economic model to maximize investment returns and attract local and international partners.

The ministry said the framework will also align with the government’s broader reform agenda, including digital transformation and modern project management systems.

The government views the Development Road Project as one of Iraq’s most important strategic investments. Officials expect it to diversify the economy beyond oil, generate new non-oil revenues, attract foreign investment, and create thousands of jobs across multiple sectors.

By leveraging Iraq’s geographic position between East and West, the project is also expected to strengthen the country’s role as a regional center for transportation, logistics, and international trade.

World.title: Iraq’s non-oil revenues jump to 16%
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Eco Iraq Observatory, which studies economic performance indicators, disclosed on Saturday that non-oil income now accounts for 16 percent of Iraq’s overall financial revenues, the highest percentage recorded so far.

According to a statement released by the observatory, this is the first time that the percentage of non-oil earnings has climbed to 16 percent during the months of May and June, having not exceeded five percent in years.

Eco Iraq noted that the proportion originally grew to roughly 10 percent between May 2020 and October 2022, then remained stable at that level during Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani’s leadership before recently hitting its peak.

The statement highlighted that non-oil revenues are divided into commodity taxes, production fees, general fees, income and wealth taxes, transfer revenues, and other sources.

Iraqi Kurdistan’s income, which it distributes to the federal government in Baghdad, accounts for around 5.5 percent of overall non-oil revenues.

As part of the government’s efforts to diversify the economy and achieve Iraq’s long-term development goals, Mazhar Saleh, the Prime Minister’s Advisor for Financial Affairs, stated in early June that an initiative would be launched. This initiative aims to create an integrated link between enhancing the structure of non-oil revenues within the framework of state finances and diversifying the non-oil GDP.

The Iraqi government established the ambitious goal, referred to as ‘Iraq 2035,’ in May. It includes both public finance reforms and social market economy policies, which aim to facilitate a gradual structural transformation of the national economy, as stated by Saleh.

The vision transforms fiscal policy to ensure that non-oil income accounts for at least 46 percent of total governmental revenues. This will improve budgetary sustainability and reduce the volatility caused by overreliance on oil earnings.

World.title: Iraq to launch ferry routes to Iran, Kuwait, UAE, and Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is preparing to launch a network of regular maritime passenger routes connecting the country with Iran, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, and Saudi Arabia, as part of a broader effort to revive the country’s maritime transport sector and strengthen regional tourism.

According to Iraq’s Ministry of Transport, the initiative will begin after technical and administrative requirements are completed in coordination with relevant authorities inside Iraq and neighboring countries.

A source at the ministry’s media office told Iraq’s official newspaper that the government has developed a comprehensive plan to operate regional maritime transport services using an expanded fleet of boats and ferries.

The ministry currently operates 40 boats and ferries under its river transport program and has recently added 15 new boats and three ferries to the fleet. The upgraded vessels are expected to provide modern, safe transportation for passengers while supporting Iraq’s growing tourism sector.

According to the ministry, most of the new vessels will be deployed on passenger and tourism routes linking Iraq with Kuwait, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Iran. Officials said services will begin once all operational approvals, safety procedures, and cross-border coordination have been finalized to ensure the routes meet international maritime safety standards.

The planned connections are expected to facilitate both tourism and commercial travel between Iraq and neighboring countries. The Ministry of Transport believes the new maritime routes will provide an affordable and practical alternative for regional travel, particularly for leisure tourism.

The project is also expected to improve mobility for official delegations and religious visitors while strengthening economic ties with Gulf states and Iran through enhanced passenger connectivity.

Officials described the initiative as a significant step toward revitalizing Iraq’s maritime transport sector after years of limited regional ferry services. The ferry project forms part of a wider government strategy to modernize Iraq’s river and maritime transport infrastructure.

Alongside expanding its fleet, the ministry is investing in the development of ports, docks, and river terminals to improve passenger services and operational efficiency.

The broader vision aims to restore river and maritime transport as an important component of Iraq’s transportation network while supporting economic development, tourism, and greater regional integration.

World.title: Kirkuk Engineers Syndicate accuses BP of sidelining local talent and demands an 85% local hiring quota
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Kirkuk Engineers Syndicate has voiced strong concerns over hiring practices and subcontract awards linked to BP’s operations in the province’s oil fields, alleging that local engineers and businesses are being overlooked in favor of workers and companies from outside Kirkuk.

While welcoming international investment in Iraq’s energy sector, the syndicate warned it would pursue legal action and peaceful protests if local employment requirements are not enforced.

In a statement, the syndicate said it is closely monitoring recruitment procedures and the awarding of secondary contracts related to BP’s projects in Kirkuk.

It argued that the current approach has resulted in several violations, including the exclusion of qualified local engineers despite the availability of experienced graduates and professionals from the province.

The syndicate also claimed that engineering and technical staff are being recruited from outside Kirkuk, while numerous subcontracting and logistics contracts have been awarded to companies based elsewhere.

According to the statement, these practices undermine the local economy and deprive Kirkuk residents of employment opportunities linked to projects operating within their province.

The syndicate stressed that Kirkuk residents bear the environmental and health impacts associated with oil production and should therefore receive priority in employment opportunities.

It called on the Ministry of Oil and the Kirkuk provincial administration to require that at least 85% of jobs across all project stages be reserved exclusively for residents of Kirkuk.

In addition, the syndicate demanded formal representation on the joint recruitment committee to ensure transparency and fairness in hiring decisions. It also urged authorities to use the syndicate’s database of registered engineering graduates when filling vacancies.

Among its proposals, the syndicate called for all job applications to be processed exclusively through the employment office of the Kirkuk Governorate, arguing that a centralized system would improve transparency and ensure equal access to opportunities.

The organization also backed government efforts to distribute employment opportunities fairly among all communities in Kirkuk without discrimination.

The statement concluded with a warning that the syndicate would not remain silent if local engineers continue to be excluded from employment opportunities.

It said it is prepared to coordinate with legislative and executive authorities and pursue all available legal avenues, alongside peaceful protests, to protect the rights of Kirkuk’s engineering community. The statement did not include a response from BP regarding the allegations.

World.title: Did you approve lethal force, pellet guns: Rahul Gandhi to Amit Shah; bill in Lok Sabha today
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

MP

shot off a letter to Union home minister

, demanding accountability for police's alleged high-handedness against protesters at Jantar Mantar, signalling a fiery start to the second week of the Monsoon session, as govt is set to table in Lok Sabha on Monday a bill that enhances punishment in cases of paper leaks as part of its raft of measures to respond to the protest.

Opposition MPs said they will finalise their stand at their strategy meeting before parliamentary proceedings begin. LS leader of the opposition Rahul's letter to Shah gave an early indication.

"As home minister, did you approve the use of lethal force including pellet guns against students? If not, who did? Are the people in plainclothes seen beating students with lathis police personnel or volunteers? Youth and students, future of our country, are demanding answers and accountability," he said, noting that security forces deployed in Delhi answer ultimately to Shah.

Govt wonât like to be seen as making direct concessions to Cong, say NDA circles

A day after education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned to pacify Cockroach Janta Party and the opposition, PM Modi said in a message to students that govt will bring to Parliament the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill as he announced a taskforce for exam reforms.

With govt determined to wrest back the initiative after making several concessions over the paper leak row and Congress and its allies keen to press home their advantage, both sides will need to come to an agreement for normal business to return to Parliament after the first weekâs washout.





The view within BJP-led NDA circles is that govt would not like to be seen making any direct concession to Congress, and instead point to the measures it has taken in the last few days.

With Modi announcing the task force, Shah said this underlines govtâs principle of constant reform to safeguard future of the new generation. âThe task force will ensure that no one can ever breach the sanctity of our exam system. We will impose exemplary punishment on culprits of paper leak and ensure no one ever dares commit this crime,â he said.

Govt has said paper leaks have happened in different states irrespective of political affiliations of govt of the day. âGovt has shown a big heart and underscored its sincerity. We are hopeful opposition will now allow a debate to take place. But if they continue to play politics, weâll hit back,â a govt functionary said.

In his letter, Rahul accused police of âbarbaric assaultâ on students during their march to Parliament on July 20. Congressâs Jairam Ramesh demanded an apology from Modi, with opposition MPs Sagarika Ghose of TMC and CPMâs John Brittas echoing the charge. The latter called for a judicial panel to inquire into the assault.

World.title: Ship with 4 Indians hit at Ukraine port; 2 safe, fate of 2 unknown
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Following the killing of five Indian nationals in the Russia-Ukraine conflict in recent days, the govt warned Indians intending to undertake employment on commercial vessels operating in or transiting the conflict-affected Black Sea region to carefully assess the prevailing security risks before accepting such assignments.

The advisory came hours after a merchant vessel carrying four Indians was struck at Ukraine's Odesa port. India's embassy in Ukraine said on Sunday that while two of the Indians were safe, information about the other two was awaited.

The incident occurred on Saturday when MV AGN Ragnar was hit at the port of Odesa, one of Ukraine's key Black Sea ports that has frequently come under attack since the outbreak of the Russia-Ukraine conflict.

The embassy said search and rescue operations were in progress and that it was in constant contact with the authorities concerned to ascertain the status of the missing crew members and provide all possible assistance.

Government asks sailors for detailed info on shipâs intended route

The MEA advisory said those who choose to undertake such employment should exercise utmost caution.

âThe security situation in and around the Black Sea and adjoining maritime areas remains highly volatile due to the ongoing conflict.





Commercial vessels operating in or transiting these waters are facing significant security risks, including missile and drone attacks,â said the ministry.

It added that since April 2026, there has been an increase in the number of such incidents on commercial vessels resulting in the loss of five Indian lives.

Govt also asked Indian nationals to obtain comprehensive information from employers/recruitment agencies and ship operators regarding the vesselâs intended route, ports of call, security arrangements, insurance coverage and emergency response procedures.

Meanwhile, urging all stakeholders to be more cautious in the light of ongoing tension across sea routes, the countryâs maritime regulator DG Shipping on Friday retweeted the advisory of Information Fusion Centre â Indian Ocean Region (IFCIOR), a 24x7 regional maritime security centre hosted by the Indian Navy.

In the post on X, IFCIOR said maritime security environment across Strait of Hormuz, Gulf of Aden, Bab-al-Mandab and Red Sea remained âhighly volatileâ, with concurrent hybrid threats, piracy activity and route-specific risks affecting commercial shipping.

World.title: CJP's win fuels call by 'E20 Janta Party' for no-ethanol option
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Inspired by Cockroach Janta Party's campaign over the NEET paper leak that led to Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as education minister, a new outfit - E20 Janta Party - has stepped into the ring, demanding consumers be given the opt-ion of buying 100% petrol and seeking the resignation of road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari.

The campaign has found support among transporters, with Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters and Tour Operators Association announcing a march to Parliament against E20 petrol on Aug 4. The association alleged that the ethanol-blending policy has reduced fuel efficiency, increased maintenance costs and affected engine performance, particularly in older vehicles.

E20 Janta Party, which gained more than 25,000 followers on X in a few hours Sunday, said it was not seeking subsidies, free fuel or withdrawal of ethanol-blended petrol, but only demanding that consumers be given the choice to buy the fuel they want.

It also demanded transparent fuel labelling so consumers knew what they were buying, publication of data on the costs, benefits and impact of fuel blends, and independent studies on mileage, engine performance, emissions and maintenance costs.

Although ethanol-free 100-octane premium petrol has long been available in the country, it is sold only at select fuel stations and costs Rs 169 per litre, compared with Rs 102.12 per litre for standard E20 fuel (in Delhi).

Minister of state for petr-oleum Suresh Gopi told Parliament last week that govt had not received "widespread or substantiated" complaints on ethanol-blended petrol affecting vehicle performance.

World.title: ‘Banned chemical’: CPCB red-flags new ‘green’ crackers
World.content:
NEW DELHI: There is no unanimity on allowing commercial production of next-generation green firecrackers in the country, with two govt organisations taking contradictory stands in

.

Council of Scientific and Industrial Research - National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI) has approved the new formulations, stating that they reduce pollution levels by 40-60%. In contrast, Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has objected, arguing that these crackers still contain barium nitrate - a chemical banned by the SC - and, therefore, cannot be permitted.

The Centre had asked CSIR-NEERI to develop green/low-emission fireworks with pollution reduction of more than 50% in association with fireworks manufacturers.

Thereafter, Tamil Nadu Fireworks and Amorces Manufacturers' Association (TANFAMA) devised new-generation fireworks formulations with reduced quantity of barium salts/nitrates in combination with other oxidisers for particulate emission reduction of more than 50%.

As per the CSIR-NEERI report, emission reductions achieved for PM10 and PM2.5 were between 45% and 60%, and recommended that these formulations for light-emission fireworks, such as flowerpots, sparklers, chakkars, pencils and twinkling stars and their hybrids, may be considered for commercial production.





It also approved manufacture of joined crackers, known as 'ladis', which have been banned as per the court's order.

The report said there was a reduction in particulate matter (PM) emissions by approximately 30% and a reduction in solid waste generation by up to 32% for joined crackers.

Responding to the CSIR-NEERI report, CPCB raised objection on how barium nitrate could be used in crackers as it was banned by the apex court and allowing their production would be in violation of the court's order.

"This court, vide order dated Oct 23, 2018, has expressly banned the use of barium salts in firecrackers and, therefore, any formulation involving barium compounds, even in reduced quantities, is in contravention of the said order," the board said.

"The reported reduction in PM10 and PM2.5 levels has not been comparatively assessed with (i) improved low-emission crackers and (ii) green crackers formulated entirely without barium, rendering the claim incomplete and inconclusive," it further said.

Caught between contradictory stands taken by two expert bodies, the ministry of environment, forest and climate change filed an affidavit bringing it to the apex court's notice and left it to the SC to take a decision on the issue. It also informed the court that the composition of new-generation firecrackers was sent to the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO), which is the regulatory body for explosive substances, and it had given a no-objection certificate to the new formulation of firecrackers.

World.title: CJP’s win fuels call by ‘E20 Janta Party’ for no-ethanol option
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Inspired by Cockroach Janta Party's successful campaign that led to Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as education minister over NEET paper leak, a new outfit -- E20 Janta Party -- has stepped into the ring, demanding that consumers be given the option of buying 100% petrol and seeking the resignation of road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari over the issue.

The campaign has found support among transporters, with Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters and Tour Operators Association announcing a march to Parliament against E20 petrol on Aug 4. The association alleged that the ethanol-blending policy has reduced fuel efficiency, increased maintenance costs and affected engine performance, particularly in older vehicles.

E20 Janta Party, which gained more than 25,000 followers on X within a few hours on Sunday, said it was not seeking subsidies, free fuel or withdrawal of ethanol-blended petrol, but only demanding that consumers be given a choice to buy the fuel they want.

"Every Indian should have the freedom to choose and purchase 100% petrol alongside blended fuel options," group said. It also demanded transparent fuel labelling so that consumers know what they are buying, publication of data on the costs, benefits and impact of different fuel blends, and independent studies on mileage, engine performance, emissions and maintenance costs.

Although ethanol-free 100-octane premium petrol has long been available in the country, it is sold only at select fuel stations and costs Rs 169 per litre, compared with Rs 102.12 per litre for standard E20 fuel (in Delhi), making it significantly expensive for most consumers. Govt recently said E20 is now the standard fuel, and there are no plans to reduce the ethanol-blending percentage.

World.title: 3 Indians die in workplace accidents in Gulf every week, shows MEA data
World.content:
HYDERABAD: Over 800 Indian expats died in workplace accidents between 2023 and 2025, according to MEA data. Of these, 55% occurred in Gulf countries, which recorded nearly three deaths a week on an average.

The latest incident â the Qatar blast that killed 12 Indians last month â has renewed calls for scrutiny of safety lapses.

According to MEA data, Saudi Arabia recorded the highest toll, with 182 deaths over the three-year period â more than one Indian worker every week â followed by UAE with 128 fatalities.

A majority of suicides during the period were also reported from Gulf nations, underscoring the challenges faced by migrant workers.

Further, to ensure womenâs safety, only state-run agencies have been authorised to recruit female workers holding ECR passports to the Gulf through the e-Migrate portal, the minister said.

Telangana NRI Migrantsâ Association attributed the recurring fatalities to multiple factors: inadequate use of safety equipment, poor adherence to workplace safety protocols, technical failures at industrial sites and insufficient skill and safety training.

Many workers, they said, labour in temperatures exceeding 45 degrees Celsius and return to accommodations cooled to 20 degrees Celsius, exposing their bodies to temperature swings of 20-25 degrees Celsius, which can lead to serious health complications.





Most Indians in the Gulf are employed in sectors like construction, retail, warehouses and automobiles, where occupational risks are high.

âAt times, workers neglect their own safety by failing to wear protective gear such as helmets, boots and gloves while working in hazardous industries. In several cases, they are unaware of the risks,â said Manda Bheem Reddy, vice-chairman, Telangana NRI Cell.

The high number of suicides, the migrantsâ welfare association said, is often driven by cramped quarters and poor-quality food, coupled with extremely hectic work schedules.

âAlso, workers often go without salaries for up to three months while putting in shifts of 12 hours a day. Even when wages are paid, deductions are common, adding to their str-ess,â said B M Vinod Kumar, chairman, Telangana govtâs NRI advisory committee.

Many employers allegedly evade responsibility by attributing workplace deaths to ânatural causesâ such as heart attacks, Vinod claimed. Only a few provide compensation through insurance coverage.

According to MEA, govt accords high priority to the safety and well-being of Indians abroad and there are channels to enable them to reach out to missions.

Kirti Vardhan Singh, minister of state for external affairs, said in Rajya Sabha that Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendras have been set up in locations such as New Delhi, Dubai, Riyadh and Jeddah. âThere are dedicated labour wings... Indian missions regularly organise open house and consular camps in remote areas to get feedback from the workers...,â she said.

Further, to ensure womenâs safety, only state-run agencies have been authorised to recruit female workers holding ECR passports to the Gulf through the e-Migrate portal, the minister said.

World.title: Opposition to take on government in Parliament over police action against protesting student
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The second week of the monsoon session of Parliament is set for a fiery start with the opposition led by the Congress set to mount its attack on the govt over the alleged police brutality against protesting students, demanding accountability and an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Leader of Opposition

set the tone by writing a letter to Home minister Amit Shah on Sunday demanding accountability for the "barbaric assault" on students who were peacefully protesting on July 20.

âOur students were demanding a fair and accountable education system. Instead of being heard, security forces assaulted them with indiscriminate force, including lethal weapons and tear gas. Hundreds have suffered serious injuries.

Women students have been assaulted by policemen, including by deliberately targeting their private parts. Most shocking has been the use of lethal pellet guns,â Gandhi said in the letter.

He went on to cite his meeting with 19 - year old student Sahil Lochab, who he said "is now in severe pain and is likely to lose an eye because he was shot with pellet gunsâ.

Security forces deployed in Delhi answer ultimately to you, so I ask, âAs Home minister, did you approve the use of lethal force including pellet guns against students? If not, who did?â

âAre the people in plain clothes seen beating students with lathis police personnel or volunteers? Who authorised their deployment?,â he asked Shah.





âYouth and students, the future of our country, are demanding answers and accountability. Their voices will be heard,â he added.

Sharing the letter, Congress general secretary, in-charge of communications, Jairam Ramesh said in a post in Hindi on X, âThe home minister must answer these crucial questions in Parliament tomorrow. The prime minister should apologise to the students."

Meanwhile, the floor strategy of the opposition and its position on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 being brought by the govt will be finalised at the INDIA bloc meeting in Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge's chamber in Parliament on Monday.

There is a strong view among INDIA bloc leaders that the demand for accountability and action against

over the action against protesting students needs to be raised strongly and the responsibility of Home Minister Amit Shah needs to be underscored.

Resonating the sentiment of the opposition, TMC's Rajya Sabhaâs deputy leader Sagarika Ghose has submitted a notice under Rule 267 seeking suspension of the day's business in the Rajya Sabha on Monday to allow an immediate discussion on the "use of excessive force on student protestors during NEET examination protests".

Ghose said the right to peaceful protest was a constitutional right, but student protesters had allegedly been subjected to "lethal and semi-lethal force" by security agencies. Her notice also raised the question as to who authorised the use of such weapons and what protocols were followed.

CPI(M) MP John Brittas said,"Everyone is anxious about the functioning of Parliament! But are we not equally outraged by the blatant violation of every rule and regulation, and the ruthless use of lethal weapons against unarmed, innocent protesters? Can the Home Minister â who is directly responsible for the Delhi Police and the administration of Delhi â simply wash his hands of this shameful and shocking episode? When such brutal atrocities are unleashed in the national capital, how can responsibility not be fixed?.

"

"Beyond fixing responsibility, a judicial commission must be immediately constituted to inquire into this assault. We possess a mountain of evidence that conclusively proves every fundamental principle of law and regulation have been trampled upon," he added.

World.title: 'Every generation of Indians qualifies as ... ': Shashi Tharoor's reply to son Ishaan's 'ban Boomers on WhatsApp' remark
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Sunday offered a witty response to his son Ishaan Tharoor's social media post calling for a ban on "boomers" using WhatsApp, adding a humorous twist to an ongoing debate over children's access to social media.

The exchange began after Ishaan reacted to Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu's suggestion that India should ban young children from using social media, similar to recently approved restrictions in France.

"I agree young kids should not be on social media at all. But India needs to ban Boomers on WhatsApp first before it does anything else," Ishaan wrote on X.

Responding to the post, Shashi Tharoor quipped, "Given our reproductive patterns, my son, unlike in the West, every generation of Indians, including yours, qualifies as [baby]Boomers!"

Debate sparked by Sridhar Vembu's proposal



The online exchange followed comments by Sridhar Vembu, who backed restrictions on children's use of social media after France passed legislation banning children under the age of 15 from accessing social media platforms and prohibiting mobile phone use in schools.

Vembu argued that young children should spend less time on digital platforms and more time engaging in outdoor activities and reading.

"India should ban social media for young children too. I believe young children should read physical books, play in the dirt under the sun, and stay away from social media!" he said.

His remarks triggered mixed reactions online, with some users supporting stricter controls on children's social media use, while others argued that such decisions should be left to parents rather than the government.





The term "boomer", originally referring to people born between 1946 and 1964 during the post-World War II baby boom, is now commonly used online as slang for older people perceived to hold outdated views or frequently offer unsolicited advice.

World.title: Search for 17 missing crew after c
World.content:
A multinational search by Vietnamese, Philippine and Chinese rescuers was underway on Sunday for 17 crew members missing after a cargo ship sank in bad weather off a Chinese-occupied shoal in the disputed South China Sea.

The Vietnamese cargo vessel Khoi Nguyen 18, carrying 62 people, sank late Saturday (July 25, 2026) near Fiery Cross Reef, which is a Chinese-built island and a military outpost in the hotly contested Spratly Islands.

Of those on board, 45 crew members have been found and 17 others are still reported missing.

The vessel “sank while operating in bad weather conditions in the East Sea,” Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Pham Thu Hang said.

The Philippine Coast Guard said it deployed a patrol vessel and an aircraft to help search for the missing crew members after receiving a request from Vietnam. Chinese rescue ships and helicopters, along with other vessels in the area, joined the operation.

Vietnamese authorities said fishing vessels had joined the search and that the families of those on board had been notified.

Philippine Coast Guard spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said that it was coordinating with Vietnam’s coast guard “for other operational information needed to guide the search and rescue response.”

She said the coast guard was also using a search planning system to improve the chances of locating the missing crew members and had issued a navigational warning urging ships transiting the area to keep watch and assist if it was safe to do so.

The Philippine Coast Guard said the operation was being conducted under international maritime agreements and bilateral cooperation with Vietnam.

Vietnam’s Foreign Ministry thanked China for its swift assistance and said it hoped the search would continue to find the remaining crew members.

China has become increasingly aggressive in asserting its claims in virtually the entire South China Sea, through which about $5 trillion in global trade transits each year. The sea passage is also believed to be sitting atop vast undersea deposits of oil and gas.

As well as China and the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Taiwan also have overlapping claims in the strategic waterway.

World.title: West Asia war updates: Iran Army says war to ‘expand further’ if U.S. attacks restart
World.content:
This live blog is closed

Iran’s Army warned on Sunday (July 26, 2026) that the war in West Asia would widen if the United States chose to press ahead with attacks on the Islamic republic, ahead of the visit of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to Washington.

The U.S. military has paused its airstrikes on Iran after nearly two weeks of intensifying bombing, while diplomatic efforts have pushed forward to try to avert a return to all-out war. Regional officials involved in the mediation efforts said that concerted diplomacy was under way and that a pause in U.S. strikes and Iranian counterstrikes on neighbouring countries hosting American forces was a “positive signal that helps their efforts to de-escalate.”

The U.S. naval blockade against Iran remains in full effect, the U.S. Central Command said early Sunday (July 26, 2026).

Despite the lull in fighting, tensions are high in the region. Yemen’s Houthi rebels said on Saturday (July 25, 2026) that they fired missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia in response to Saudi airstrikes on the strategic Red Sea city of Hodeida. The Iran-backed rebels say they have closed the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which has become even more vital for Saudi oil exports since the disruption of the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: CM Suvendu Adhikari meets victims of Sundarbans Trawler capsize, calls for stepping up disaster management preparedness
World.content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (July 26, 2026) met the victims of the Sundarbans trawler capsize tragedy earlier this month and announced several steps for better disaster management preparedness in the coastal areas.

At least 11 fishermen were found dead while four others are still missing after a trawler from Purba Medinipur capsized on July 8, 2026. It lost communication soon after setting off and remained missing till it was traced by the Coastal Guards on July 14, 2026, at c Officials said the fishermen in the trawler were from Digha, Nadia, Howrah, and East Medinipur in West Bengal, and from Odisha.

Soon after the incident, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a ₹2 lakh ex-gratia for each of their family members from the National Relief Fund. Meanwhile, on Wednesday (July 22, 2026), CM Adhikari also announced an ex-gratia of ₹5 lakh and a civic volunteer job for one eligible member of the family.

On Sunday (July 26, 2026), Mr. Adhikari met the families of the victims. “Many such incidents took place earlier but the government never cared about them. Our government did. We feel that it is our responsibility,” he said.

In view of the poor status of the coastal police stations, the CM declared to appoint efficient police officials in those stations immediately. They will also supported with advanced technology.

“I have also asked the disaster management department to form a 50-member Quick Response Team for Digha and surrounding coastal areas so that they can respond to any difficult situation promptly and as soon as possible,” he said.

World.title: Student organisations look to carry Jantar Mantar momentum into DUSU election
World.content:
With the Jantar Mantar protest drawing to a close, student organisations are preparing to shift their campaign from the protest site to the Delhi University campus as the new academic session begins on Tuesday.

The networking, visibility, and political momentum built during the 36-day agitation at Jantar Mantar, led by students and the Cockroach Janta Party over the NEET paper leak case, are likely to shape their outreach ahead of the DU Students’ Union (DUSU) elections. The polls are due to be held six to eight weeks after the commencement of the session, in accordance with the Lyngdoh Committee guidelines.

What set this year’s outreach apart was that it began well before the academic session. At Jantar Mantar, student organisations picked up incoming DU students from railway stations, helped them reach the protest site, distributed food and water, managed logistics, and addressed gatherings, combining political mobilisation with assistance typically associated with the DUSU election season.

Multiple student organisations maintained a visible presence at the protest site through tents and help desks. Leaders of the All India Students’ Association (AISA) emerged as prominent faces during the hunger strike, while the All India Students’ Federation ran a bookstall at the centre of the site. Volunteers from Aam Aadmi Party’s (AAP) Association of Students for Alternative Politics (ASAP), the Krantikari Yuva Sangathan and the Students’ Federation of India helped manage logistics.

The Congress-backed National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) publicly joined the protest after the alleged police violence during the July 20 protest march to Parliament. The only prominent student organisation absent from the site was the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), which said it was working for reform on campus and was present where it “needed to be”.

At present, three of the four DUSU office-bearers, including president Aryan Mann, are from the ABVP. One is from the NSUI. However, student organisations claimed that the “clear student anger against the Right” would change the course of the upcoming election.

Anjali, an AISA leader and DU student who emerged as one of the prominent faces of the protest, said, “Some of the most important issues in the country were raised at Jantar Mantar. We have anyway been raising issues about the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020. We will definitely centre our DUSU campaign around this.”

In the long run, AISA intends to “tap into the resistance and understand what caused so much anger”, she said.

NSUI national president Vinod Jakhar said the organisation had initially launched its own movement and was mobilising students across the country over the NEET paper leak issue.

“We did not get permission at Jantar Mantar, so we supported the movement in the background. Eventually, after the police violence, we joined because it was not about one organisation; it was about the students,” he said, adding that the organisation was simultaneously setting up help desks to assist students with hostel-related and other campus issues.

Sources in AAP said its students’ organisation would contest the election this year.

“There is a lot of anti-BJP sentiment among students. There will be a cultural shift in the upcoming student elections,” a source said, adding that ASAP teams had played a “significant role” at Jantar Mantar in providing security, distributing food and water, and managing the stage.

Meanwhile, the ABVP argued that it had been equally active on the issue of educational reform.

“We conducted the first major NEET protest outside the National Testing Agency (NTA), and we were looking at solutions beyond a resignation. We were thinking practically, not politically,” an ABVP member said, requesting anonymity.

He added, “Students know that we were where we needed to be: on campus. We could not join such a movement because anti-national elements were present.”

World.title: Outstation students lament fewer holiday spells in DU this year
World.content:
For Delhi University students from outside the city, academic breaks are often the only window to travel home. But with a tighter academic calendar and fewer extended holidays in the new session, many said they are finding it difficult to plan trips around classes, assignments, and attendance requirements.

The newly issued academic calendar has drawn criticism for providing limited breaks during major festivals. The week-long Deepavali break has been removed, with a holiday only on the day of the festival, which falls on a Sunday this year. For Navratri, which begins on October 11, holidays have been granted only from October 18, covering Ashtami, Navami and Dasara.

The winter break is scheduled from December 25 to 31 – seven days – with the even semester beginning on January 1, 2027, leaving little time for students to travel, celebrate, and return. “For students coming from far-off States, this is not practical,” said Arnav Vaid, a BCom student at Hansraj College from Jammu and Kashmir. “With ticket prices so high, we cannot spend ₹10,000 to ₹15,000 for a break of just five to seven days.”

72 holidays this year

According to the academic calendar, the total number of holidays stands at 72 days this year, compared to 71 days last year. However, students note that in practice, holidays are often reduced. In the 2025–26 session, although 71 days were scheduled, students effectively received 53 days due to extended examinations and delayed breaks.

University officials, however, said the calendar has been framed in accordance with University Grants Commission norms. “There have to be 90 teaching days per semester, which we are following,” an official said.

A faculty member involved in preparing timetables, speaking on condition of anonymity, said provisions exist to revise holidays later. “There is one day for Deepavali now, and more days might be added later as the university has the provision to do so. This is done later in the year after examination days are calculated,” the faculty member said. Since the Common University Entrance Test became the basis of admissions in 2022–23, delays in the NTA-led process have pushed back sessions. In 2022, undergraduate classes began in November, nearly three months later than usual.

Students also point to the university’s past record of deviating from its own calendar. In the 2025–26 session, theory examinations were held on January 1, 2026, and classes resumed the next day, effectively eliminating the winter break despite the calendar indicating a break from December 28 to January 1. In practice, the winter break was reduced further depending on exam schedules, leaving some students with little or no break at all.

Tusti Mehra, a History student at Lady Shri Ram College, said frequent revisions to the calendar add to the uncertainty. “Revised schedules are often issued just weeks in advance, forcing students to cancel travel plans, which leads to financial losses as well as emotional stress,” she said.

“Within such a short time frame, it is difficult to unwind or prepare for the next semester,” said Pavani Chourasia, a third-year History student at Hindu College, adding that shorter breaks also limit opportunities for winter internships.

Structural Issues

Faculty members, however, say the issue reflects structural constraints rather than administrative disregard. Abha Dev Habib, a professor at Miranda House, said starting the academic session on July 28 could mean that admissions are still underway when classes begin.

“Students admitted in later rounds may already be behind academically,” she said. “While aligning the calendar is important, the transition needs to be managed carefully.”

She added that accommodating extended festival breaks may not be feasible for a central university of this scale. “With a student population running into lakhs, it is difficult to account for every regional festival. Even a mid-semester break could become disruptive depending on when festivals fall,” she said.

World.title: Finding land biggest challenge for Kozhikode Corporation’s stray dog shelter project
World.content:
Animal welfare organisations have welcomed the Kozhikode Corporation’s decision to invite expressions of interest (EOIs) from individuals and organisations willing to establish and operate shelters for street dogs as part of its efforts to find a lasting solution to the stray dog menace within the city limits. However, they cautioned that identifying suitable land for the shelters would be the biggest challenge.

The decision was taken at a meeting of officials, public representatives and members of animal welfare organisations convened by Mayor O. Sadasivan recently. The meeting discussed a series of scientific and humane measures to address the issue.

Officials said the project would initially be implemented on a pilot basis by establishing several small shelters at different locations, each capable of accommodating at least 10 street dogs. Individuals and organisations from outside the Corporation limits would also be eligible to submit proposals.

A three-member committee will be constituted to identify aggressive stray dogs and facilitate their relocation to the shelters.

“NGOs have assured the Corporation that they can take care of feeding the dogs shifted to these shelters. If required, the Corporation will also extend the necessary support. We believe this collaborative approach will make the project more practical and sustainable,” an official said.

In a statement, Mr. Sadasivan said the meeting had also decided to identify a suitable site for a larger shelter capable of accommodating more animals in the future.

“The Corporation is focussing on developing sustainable, long-term solutions rather than temporary measures to address the stray dog menace. The initiatives seek to ensure public safety while safeguarding animal welfare and will be implemented with public cooperation,” he said.

A recent survey by National Service Scheme (NSS) volunteers from the College of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Pookode, estimated that there are 28,510 street dogs within the Corporation limits.

Representatives of animal welfare organisations said they supported the civic body’s initiative but stressed that finding appropriate locations remained the biggest hurdle.

“I attended the meeting. It witnessed fruitful discussions, and we welcome the decisions taken. Everyone is willing to establish and operate shelters for stray dogs. However, the biggest challenge is finding suitable land. Even if land is identified and a shelter is proposed, residents are likely to object. To a certain extent, their concerns are understandable. The success of the initiative will depend on identifying suitable sites,” said Sudina Anuraj Varma, a member of People For Animals.

Ms. Varma said relocating all stray dogs within the Corporation limits to shelters was neither feasible nor desirable. “Instead, the shelters should primarily accommodate abandoned pet dogs, particularly aggressive animals, those showing symptoms of rabies, dogs suffering from diseases such as distemper, severely debilitated animals, and dogs injured in accidents,” she added.

The Corporation also decided to organise special ward-level camps to streamline the licensing and microchipping of pet dogs.

World.title: RBI sees rupee as undervalued; FCNR(B) inflows cross $32 billion
World.content:
The Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) recent measures to attract foreign capital have garnered strong investor response, with banks mobilising nearly $32 billion, largely through Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) or FCNR(B) deposits, while government securities have attracted more than $7 billion in foreign inflows since the June policy measures, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra has said.

Also read | Examining the RBI’s remittances survey

In an interview with The Hindu BusinessLine, Mr. Malhotra dismissed concerns that the inflows merely represent a recycling of existing deposits. He added that the RBI has adequate tools to manage any resulting liquidity. The inflows have strengthened India’s external position amid heightened geopolitical uncertainty and volatile global capital flows, he said.

Responding to concerns over the RBI bearing the hedging cost of fresh FCNR(B) deposits and offering concessional forex swaps for external commercial borrowings (ECBs) by public sector entities, Mr. Malhotra said: “It is not something which should be a matter of concern because we have a foolproof system of insuring ourselves. So, whatever dollars we get, the excess foreign currency is invested in foreign assets. The risk, therefore, is not there.”

The Governor said the measures should be viewed in the context of challenging global conditions facing emerging markets and are expected to further strengthen India’s balance of payments and currency stability.

Mr. Malhotra also sought to reassure markets on the rupee, arguing that recent depreciation does not reflect any weakness in the country’s economic fundamentals. According to him, pressure on the currency has largely stemmed from geopolitical tensions, dollar strength and broader volatility across emerging markets.

“We do not target any specific exchange rate or band for the rupee. Our intervention, whenever necessary, is targeted to curb excessive volatility,” he said, adding that the currency is “not overvalued” and could even be considered undervalued in both nominal and real effective exchange rate terms.

He cited the current account surplus during April-May, robust services exports, resilient remittance inflows, rising merchandise exports and improving foreign direct investment flows as indicators of the strength of the external sector.

Forex management

On forex reserve management, Mr. Malhotra said the RBI continues to be guided by the principles of safety, liquidity and returns, while reviewing reserve deployment periodically.

Turning to monetary policy, the Governor reiterated that inflation control remains the RBI’s foremost priority even as it remains mindful of growth risks. He said the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) will continue to adopt a data-dependent approach while navigating the evolving growth-inflation trade-off.

“Our primary mandate is inflation and price stability. Therefore, we will do whatever is required first, to keep price stability and then, to see to what extent we can support growth,” he said.

While inflation has moved above the 4% midpoint of the MPC’s target band, Mr. Malhotra indicated that policymakers do not yet see signs of broad-based price pressures becoming entrenched.

On policy rate

Mr. Malhotra defended the current policy rate, saying it reflects prevailing growth-inflation dynamics and elevated global uncertainties. The MPC’s neutral stance, he noted, provides flexibility to maintain the status quo or move rates in either direction depending on incoming data, with decisions guided by domestic conditions rather than policy actions of global central banks.

The Governor downplayed concerns that strong credit growth could lead to overheating, arguing that credit creation generates deposits while capital adequacy, liquidity coverage and stable funding ratios remain the key constraints on lending. He added that Indian banks remain well positioned on these parameters.

Addressing governance issues, Mr. Malhotra said the RBI’s regulatory and supervisory framework remains robust, while growing foreign interest in Indian banks and NBFCs reflects confidence in the country’s financial system and long-term growth prospects. Ownership norms, he added, will continue to emphasise fit-and-proper criteria and diversified shareholding structures.

(The writers are with the Hindu BusinessLine)

World.title: Odisha BJP leaders criticise post by MP’s daughter on Pradhan
World.content:
A social media post of Bhubaneswar MP Aparajita Sarangi's daughter Archita Sachin Rahar allegedly celebrating the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as the Union Education Minister has sparked resentment in the party rank and file in Odisha.

Ms. Rahar, in an Instagram post which had a photograph of Mr. Pradhan in the backdrop of the national flag, wrote, “Dharmendra Pradhan resigns amid massive student protests over NEET leak fiasco.” State BJP leaders, including her mother, on the other hand, expressed sympathy for Mr. Pradhan.

Ms. Sarangi, a two-time MP from Bhubaneswar, was, however, unavailable for comment. Sources said the lawmaker had asked her daughter to remove the post after getting a phone call from Mr. Pradhan’s office. However, it failed to have an impact.

BJP leaders criticised Ms. Rahar over her post. Jagannath Pradhan, a BJP leader, said, “Mr. Pradhan is son of the soil. His resignation has hurt us. Odias have welcomed the daughter of Bihar [Aparajita] and made her MP twice.”

“Ms. Sarangi should have control over her family members. She should tender an apology to Odisha for her daughter making adverse remarks against Mr. Pradhan,” he added.

World.title: Raja Muthupandi wins silver in 65kg weighlifting, India’s fourth medal at CWG 2026
World.content:
Raja Muthupandi won India’s fourth medal of the 2026 Commonwealth Games, and third in weightlifting, by winning silver in men’s 65kg late on the fourth day in Glasgow. Muthupandi had a best lift of 126kg in snatch and 160kg in clean and jerk. His total lift was 286kg. Malaysia’s Aznil Bidin won gold with a Games record lift of 299kg while Papua New Guinea’s Morea Baru won bronze with 282kg at the SEC Armadillo.



It is India’s third medal in weightlifting and fourth overall at Glasgow 2026. Rishikanta Singh had won silver earlier in the day in men’s 60kg while Mirabai Chanu later won an incredible third consecutive CWG gold in women’s 48kg. The medal marks a remarkable turnaround for Muthupandi, who has dealt with a host of injury and health setbacks in recent years. He secured a flight to Glasgow by winning the national title and setting a new national record.

World.title: Berlin Pride attack suspect shot dead after 24-hour manhunt
World.content:
A man suspected of driving a minivan into a crowd near Berlin’s Pride festival that killed at least one person and injured 29 others was shot dead by police in the city’s Spandau district, German officials said on Sunday.

Abdul Ballout, a German citizen with Lebanese heritage, was killed following a manhunt launched by Berlin police for nearly 24 hours after the attack in downtown Berlin. Prosecutors said he had previously sought to join the militant Islamic State group, AP reported.

Gegen 18 Uhr konnte der Tatverdächtige des gestrigen Anschlags im Großen Tiergarten in einer Kleingartenanlage in #Spandau lokalisiert werden. Nach bisherigen Erkenntnissen soll er mit einer Stichwaffe auf unsere Einsatzkräfte zugelaufen sein, daraufhin kam es zum polizeilichen… pic.twitter.com/ncslEZom7N — Polizei Berlin (@polizeiberlin) July 26, 2026

Police say suspect charged at officers with knife

Informing about the encounter, Berlin police wrote on X, “Around 6 pm (1600 GMT), the suspect involved in yesterday’s attack in Tiergarten was located at an allotment garden complex in Spandau.”



Police search the area after a deadly incident in which a vehicle crashed into a crowd near Berlin’s annual Christopher Street Day Pride parade. (Photo: Reuters) Police search the area after a deadly incident in which a vehicle crashed into a crowd near Berlin’s annual Christopher Street Day Pride parade. (Photo: Reuters)

A federal prosecutor confirmed that one person has been shot and declared dead. Berlin police identified the deceased as Abdul B, 21, and published his picture, asking the public for information on his whereabouts.

“According to initial findings, he ran towards officers while armed with a bladed weapon; police… subsequently opened fire. Despite immediate resuscitation efforts by the Berlin Fire Department, he died at the scene,” the police said.

Authorities cite alleged Islamist links

Abdul, who was born in Germany in 2005, was suspected of driving the vehicle into a crowd celebrating one of Europe’s largest Pride events on Saturday night. He later stabbed others with a machete, with a German minister describing the act as an “Islamist attack”.

Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said the suspect had “attracted attention in the past through a high number of criminal offences, through radicalisation, through membership of the Islamist scene,” Reuters reported.



Attack renews security debate in Germany

The incident was the latest in a spate of vehicle attacks on crowds in Germany in recent times, which has also triggered discussions around security and immigration.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, ahead of a memorial service at St Mary’s Church in Berlin, urged German residents to protect liberal values.

“We will defend the freedom, openness, and liberal spirit of our lives and our society with everything we can do,” Merz added.

World.title: ‘Congress backed from outside, credit goes to youth’: Revanth Reddy on CJP protest
World.content:
Telangana will pass a resolution in the Legislative Assembly in August, recommending reducing the minimum age for Lok Sabha membership to 21 from the current 25, Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy said on Sunday.

While suggesting those aged 21 and above should be eligible to contest elections to Lok Sabha and state assemblies, the Telangana CM also said the minimum age requirement for Rajya Sabha and state Legislative Council memberships should be 25 instead of the current 30.



Reddy said he would submit a representation to Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, stating that a revised minimum age Bill be introduced, at least as a private Bill, in Parliament. He said the Centre’s ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) should consider bringing this Bill up for discussion in the ongoing session of Parliament.

World.title: UTT final: Manush Shah’s masterclass powers U Mumba to back-to-back titles
World.content:
U Mumba TT started the season with heavy defeats to Dempo Goa Challengers (5-10) and Ahmedabad APL Pipers (6-9) and nearly faced three straight losses. Anusha Kutumbale had ensured that did not happen, breaking the streak with a clutch golden point win over Dabang Delhi TTC, then repeated her heroics on Sunday to secure U Mumba’s second consecutive Ultimate Table Tennis (UTT) title.

At the receiving end were the same Goan team who were undefeated going into the final. They fell prey to Manush Shah’s all-round brilliance on the second evening running, before Kutumbale finished things off calmly.

Captain Manush had won the singles and mixed doubles rubbers on Saturday to fashion U Mumba’s semi-final triumph over HVR Kolkata Thunder Blades. He did the same in the final, usurping five of six possible points in the matches he played as the defending champions pipped Goa 8-5 in a tantalising tie.

Just like their story in the league phase, U Mumba started the summit clash too with back-to-back defeats. Lilian Bardet and Anna Hursey were on the wrong side of two riveting singles matches, with Abhinandh PB and Bernadette Szocs shining through.

Having blanked Bardet 3-0 in the league phase on the back of inside-out crosscourt forehand drives, Abhinandh came out with a different strategy against him in the final. The 18-year-old chose to attack Bardet’s forehand and body down the middle, and the Frenchman had few answers in Game 1.



The senior pro, called ‘T-Rex’ for his victory celebration style, upped the ante with powerful inside-out forehands of his own early in the second game. But the Chennai lad responded beautifully with a mix of short and long third-ball attacks, winning nine out of 10 points from 1-5 down. It was a sight to behold as Abhinandh remained dauntless amid scoreboard pressure, delighting the partisan crowd with his aesthetically pleasing shots.

Abhinandh later thanked his coaches for helping him build mental composure for times like these. “Many times before I had panicked, but I’ve worked hard on my mental strength in the last one year with my coaches,” he said.

The match was lost, but Bardet managed to wrest the initiative in the last game to snatch a crucial point for U Mumba.



The second match pitted league veteran Szocs versus the in-form Hursey. The players, bearing similar styles and evenly matched on paper, produced a duel worth the billing.

Hursey, arguably the best women’s singles player on show this season with six wins and one loss amid illness, ran away with Game 1. The better-ranked Szocs (world number 24 as against Hursey’s 34) used all her experience to fight back superbly in the next two games. She repeatedly used her tomahawk serve to induce loose returns, and pounced on them with glee.

The rallies lengthened as the match wore on, but ‘Bernie’ prevailed in more counter punches, and kept letting out roars before clinching it 5-11, 11-7, 11-7. She then explained the rationale behind her vociferous display.



“This was the only match I was playing in the final; I was not playing the mixed doubles rubber. I had a lot of pressure on me, a lot of emotions. When I won points, I let out some of that emotion. So I screamed like crazy in the latter points.”

But the 20-year-old Hursey soon redeemed herself in the mixed doubles alongside a charged-up Manush. They one-upped Alvaro Robles and Syndrela Das in straight games (11-8, 11-7, 11-9). The match was far closer than the scoreline suggested, and it was Hursey-Manush’s ability to land the top-spin winners in the corners on the vital points that shaped the result.

Manush was only half done. He took on Alvaro Robles in a fourth rubber that proved decisive to the contest.



The battle of the southpaws opened up fresh angles on the table. Manush, like he did the previous night against Ankur Bhattacharjee, moved swiftly in anticipation of returns and kept lining up his forehand. He targeted all parts of the court as per the situation, and was not averse to directing traffic at Robles’ body.

The Spaniard, though he took Game 1 with an emphatic 11-6 margin, started coming up short when initiating attacks in long rallies. Manush took charge. By snaring the golden point in the second game, he swung the match and the tie’s momentum Mumbai’s way.

By the end of this match, U Mumba needed just one more point. Kutumbale delivered it right away against the rising young Syndrela, just like she had against Delhi to spark their victory juggernaut.

World.title: London’s Gatwick Airport hit by major water outage; toilets, restaurants shut
World.content:
A major water supply failure has hit London’s Gatwick Airport, disrupting access to working toilets, bars and restaurants on Sunday, airport authorities said in a statement on X.

The UK’s second-busiest airport in Sussex lost running water at both its terminals, with passengers complaining online that they were unable to wash their hands, get hot drinks, or fill up water bottles at Gatwick Airport, The Guardian reported.

According to water suppliers, the issue also had a wider impact on Sussex and Kent areas on Sunday. A BBC report quoted people who said there was confusion and frustration at the airport as all restaurants and bars were shut, while queues built up outside toilets.
